sentences.zh: 方技下

translations.literal: Medicine and divination, part two.
translations.idiomatic: Medicine and Divination, Part Two

sentences.zh: ○賀蘭棲真柴通玄甄棲真楚衍僧誌言僧懷丙許希龐安時錢乙僧智緣郭天信魏漢津王老誌王仔昔林靈素皇甫坦王克明莎衣道人孫守榮

translations.literal: He Lanqizhen, Chai Tongxuan, Zhen Qizhen, Chu Yan, Monk Zhiyan, Monk Huaibing, Xu Xi, Pang Anshi, Qian Yi, Monk Zhiyuan, Guo Tianxin, Wei Hanjin, Wang Laozhi, Wang Zixi, Lin Lingsu, Huang Futan, Wang Keming, the Sha-robe Daoist, Sun Shourong.
translations.idiomatic: He Lanqizhen, Chai Tongxuan, Zhen Qizhen, Chu Yan, the monk Zhiyan, the monk Huaibing, Xu Xi, Pang Anshi, Qian Yi, the monk Zhiyuan, Guo Tianxin, Wei Hanjin, Wang Laozhi, Wang Zixi, Lin Lingsu, Huang Futan, Wang Keming, the Sha-robe Daoist, and Sun Shourong.

sentences.zh: 賀蘭棲真，不知何許人。

translations.literal: He Lanqizhen—his place of origin is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: He Lanqizhen was a man of unknown origin.

sentences.zh: 為道士，自言百歲。

translations.literal: He became a Daoist priest and claimed to be a hundred years old.
translations.idiomatic: He took orders as a Daoist and said he was a hundred years old.

sentences.zh: 善服氣，不憚寒暑，往往不食。

translations.literal: He was skilled at breath cultivation, unafraid of cold or heat, and often went without food.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in breath cultivation, he was indifferent to cold and heat and often ate nothing at all.

sentences.zh: 或時縱酒，遊市廛間，能啖肉至數斤。

translations.literal: At times he would indulge in wine, wander through the market streets, and could eat several jin of meat.
translations.idiomatic: Now and then he would drink freely, roam the marketplaces, and devour several jin of meat at a sitting.

sentences.zh: 始居嵩山紫虛觀，後徙濟源奉仙觀，張齊賢與之善。

translations.literal: At first he lived at the Purple Void Abbey on Mount Song; later he moved to the Offerings-to-Immortals Abbey at Jiyuan. Zhang Qixian was on friendly terms with him.
translations.idiomatic: He first resided at the Purple Void Abbey on Mount Song, then moved to the Offerings-to-Immortals Abbey at Jiyuan, where Zhang Qixian became his friend.

sentences.zh: 景德二年，詔曰：“師棲身岩壑，抗誌煙霞，觀心眾妙之門，脫屣浮雲之外。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingde, an edict said: "Master, you dwell in cliffs and ravines, hold your will aloft among mist and clouds, contemplate the gate of all wonders in the heart, and cast off your shoes beyond the floating clouds.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingde (1005), an edict read: "Master, you dwell among cliffs and ravines, your spirit set against mist and sunset glow; you contemplate the gate of all mysteries within the heart and have cast off worldly trappings as one casts off shoes beyond the drifting clouds.

sentences.zh: 朕奉希夷而為教，法清靜以臨民，思得有道之人，訪以無為之理。

translations.literal: We take the rare and subtle as our teaching and govern the people by the law of purity and stillness; we wish to obtain a man of the Way and inquire of him the principle of non-action.
translations.idiomatic: We take the rare and subtle as our doctrine and rule the people through purity and stillness; we seek a man of the Way with whom to discuss the principle of non-action.

sentences.zh: 久懷上士，欲覿真風，爰命使車，往申禮聘。

translations.literal: Long have we cherished the highest gentleman and wished to behold the true wind; therefore we now dispatch envoys to extend a ritual invitation.
translations.idiomatic: Long have we cherished the highest sage and wished to meet the true Way in person; we therefore send envoys to offer you a formal invitation.

sentences.zh: 師其暫別林穀，來儀闕庭，必副招延，無憚登涉。

translations.literal: Master, for a time leave the forested valleys, come to grace the court, surely answer our summons, and do not shrink from the journey.
translations.idiomatic: Master, leave the wooded valleys for a time and come to the imperial court; answer our summons and do not hesitate to make the journey.

sentences.zh: 今遣入內內品李懷贇召師赴闕。

translations.literal: We now send the Inner Palace attendant of the inner rank Li Huaizan to summon the Master to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: We now send the Inner Palace attendant Li Huaizan to summon you to court.

sentences.zh: ”既至，真宗作二韻詩賜之，號宗玄大師，賚以紫服、白金、茶、帛、香、藥，特蠲觀之田租，度其侍者。

translations.literal: " When he arrived, Emperor Zhenzong composed a two-rhyme poem and bestowed it on him, gave him the title Great Master Zongxuan, and rewarded him with purple robes, white gold, tea, silks, incense, and medicines; he specially remitted the abbey's land tax and ordained his attendants.
translations.idiomatic: " When he arrived, Emperor Zhenzong wrote him a couplet in regulated verse, granted him the title Great Master Zongxuan, and presented purple robes, white gold, tea, silks, incense, and medicines; he also remitted the abbey's land tax and ordained his attendants.

sentences.zh: 未幾，求還舊居。

translations.literal: Before long he asked to return to his former residence.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he asked to return to his former home.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符三年卒，時大雪，經三日，頂猶熱，人多異之。

translations.literal: He died in the third year of Dazhong Xiangfu. It was snowing heavily; after three days his crown was still warm, and many regarded this as strange.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Dazhong Xiangfu (1010) amid heavy snow; three days later the crown of his head was still warm, and many took this as a marvel.

sentences.zh: 紫通玄，字又玄，陝州閿鄉人。

translations.literal: Zi Tongxuan, style Youxuan, was a native of Minxiang in Shaanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chai Tongxuan, whose style was Youxuan, came from Minxiang in Shaan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 為道士於承天觀。

translations.literal: He was a Daoist priest at the Abbey of Receiving Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He was a Daoist at the Abbey of Receiving Heaven.

sentences.zh: 年百餘歲，善辟穀長嘯，唯飲酒。

translations.literal: He was over a hundred years old, skilled at grain avoidance and long whistling, and drank only wine.
translations.idiomatic: He was said to be over a hundred years old, practiced grain avoidance and long whistling, and drank nothing but wine.

sentences.zh: 言唐末事，曆曆可聽。

translations.literal: When he spoke of events at the end of Tang, each detail was clear and worth hearing.
translations.idiomatic: When he spoke of the late Tang, every detail rang true.

sentences.zh: 太宗召至闕下，懇求歸本觀。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong summoned him to the capital, but he earnestly begged to return to his home abbey.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong summoned him to court, but he pleaded earnestly to return to his abbey.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，屢來京師。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong took the throne, he came to the capital many times.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhenzong's accession he visited the capital repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 召對，語無文飾，多以修身慎行為說。

translations.literal: Summoned for audience, his speech had no literary ornament; he mostly spoke of cultivating the self and acting with caution.
translations.idiomatic: When summoned to audience he spoke plainly, without literary ornament, and mostly urged self-cultivation and prudent conduct.

sentences.zh: 祀汾陰，召至行在，命坐，問以無為之要。

translations.literal: When sacrificing at Fenyin, he was summoned to the imperial camp, given a seat, and asked about the essentials of non-action.
translations.idiomatic: During the sacrifice at Fenyin he was summoned to the imperial camp, seated, and questioned on the essentials of non-action.

sentences.zh: 所居觀即唐軒遊宮，有明皇詩石及所書《道德經》二碑。

translations.literal: The abbey where he lived had been Tang's Palace of Lofty Excursions; there were stone tablets with poems by Emperor Minghuang and two steles of the Daodejing in his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: His abbey had been the Tang Palace of Lofty Excursions; it held stone tablets inscribed with poems by Emperor Xuanzong and two steles bearing the Daodejing in the emperor's own calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 上作二韻詩賜之，並賚以茶、藥、束帛。

translations.literal: The emperor composed a two-rhyme poem and bestowed it on him, also rewarding him with tea, medicines, and bundles of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote him a couplet in regulated verse and also gave him tea, medicines, and silks.

sentences.zh: 詔為修道院，蠲其田租，度弟子二人。

translations.literal: An edict renamed it the Abbey of Cultivating the Way, remitted its land tax, and ordained two disciples.
translations.idiomatic: By edict it was renamed the Abbey of Cultivating the Way; its land tax was remitted and two disciples were ordained.

sentences.zh: 明年春，通玄作遺表，自稱羅山太一洞主，遣弟子張守元、李守一詣闕，以龜鶴為獻；

translations.literal: The next spring Tongxuan drew up a final memorial, styled himself Lord of the Great Unity Grotto on Mount Luo, and sent disciples Zhang Shouyuan and Li Shouyi to court to present turtles and cranes as tribute;
translations.idiomatic: The following spring Tongxuan composed a final memorial, styled himself Lord of the Great Unity Grotto on Mount Luo, and sent his disciples Zhang Shouyuan and Li Shouyi to court with turtles and cranes as tribute;

sentences.zh: 又召官僚士庶言生死之要。

translations.literal: he also summoned officials, gentry, and commoners to speak on the essentials of life and death.
translations.idiomatic: he also gathered officials, scholars, and commoners to discourse on the essentials of life and death.

sentences.zh: 夜分，盥濯，然香庭中，望闕而坐，遲明卒。

translations.literal: At midnight he washed, burned incense in the courtyard, sat facing the palace gate, and died at daybreak.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight he bathed, burned incense in the courtyard, sat facing the imperial palace, and died at daybreak.

sentences.zh: 時又召河中草澤劉巽、華山隱士鄭隱、敷水隱士李寧。

translations.literal: At the same time the court also summoned Liu Xun, a commoner recluse of Hezhong; Zheng Yin, a hermit of Mount Hua; and Li Ning, a hermit of Fushui.
translations.idiomatic: About the same time the court also summoned Liu Xun, a recluse of the Hezhong region; Zheng Yin, a hermit of Mount Hua; and Li Ning, a hermit of Fushui.

sentences.zh: 巽年七十餘，以經傳講授，躬耕自給。

translations.literal: Xun was over seventy and lectured on the classics; he farmed with his own hands to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was over seventy, taught the classics, and supported himself by farming.

sentences.zh: 授大理評事致仕，賜綠袍、笏、銀帶。

translations.literal: He was appointed Retired Grand Council Assessor of Dali, and given a green robe, tablet, and silver belt.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the retired rank of Grand Council Assessor of Dali and presented with a green robe, court tablet, and silver belt.

sentences.zh: 隱以經術為業，遇道士傳辟穀煉氣之法，修習頗驗，居華山王刁岩逾二十年，冬夏裳衣皮裘。

translations.literal: Yin took classical learning as his profession; he met a Daoist who transmitted methods of grain avoidance and refining breath, and his practice proved quite effective. He lived at Wangdiao Cliff on Mount Hua for more than twenty years, wearing fur in winter and summer alike.
translations.idiomatic: Yin made classical learning his livelihood; a Daoist taught him grain avoidance and breath cultivation, and his practice proved effective. He dwelt at Wangdiao Cliff on Mount Hua for more than twenty years, wearing furs winter and summer alike.

sentences.zh: 寧精於藥術，老而不衰，常以藥施人，人以金帛為報，輒拒之。

translations.literal: Ning was expert in pharmacy; though old he did not decline. He often gave medicines to others, but when people offered gold and silk in return he always refused.
translations.idiomatic: Ning was expert in medicine and remained vigorous in old age; he often gave medicines away, but always refused when people offered gold or silk in return.

sentences.zh: 景德中，萬安太后不豫，驛召寧赴闕，未至而後崩。

translations.literal: During Jingde, when Empress Dowager Wan'an fell ill, Ning was summoned post-haste to court, but before he arrived the empress dowager had already died.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingde era, when Empress Dowager Wan'an fell ill, Ning was summoned urgently to court, but she died before he arrived.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符四年，賜號正晦先生。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dazhong Xiangfu he was granted the title Master Zhenghui.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Dazhong Xiangfu (1011) he was granted the title Master Zhenghui.

sentences.zh: 上並作詩為賜，加以茶、藥、繒帛。

translations.literal: The emperor composed poems for each and bestowed them, adding tea, medicines, and silks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote poems for each of them and also gave tea, medicines, and silks.

sentences.zh: 獨隱辭賜物不受。

translations.literal: Yin alone declined the gifts and would not accept them.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yin refused the gifts.

sentences.zh: 甄棲真，字道淵，單州單父人。

translations.literal: Zhen Qizhen, style Daoyuan, was a native of Shanfu in Shan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen Qizhen, whose style was Daoyuan, came from Shanfu in Shan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 博涉經傳，長於詩賦。

translations.literal: He was broadly versed in the classics and commentaries and excelled at poetry and rhapsody.
translations.idiomatic: He was widely read in the classics and excelled at poetry and fu.

sentences.zh: 一應進士舉，不中第，歎曰：“勞神敝精，以追虛名，無益也。

translations.literal: Once he sat for the jinshi examination but failed to pass. He sighed and said, "To weary the spirit and exhaust the essence in pursuit of empty fame is of no use.
translations.idiomatic: He once took the jinshi examination but failed. He sighed and said, "To weary mind and spirit chasing empty fame is pointless.

sentences.zh: ”遂棄其業，讀道家書以自樂。

translations.literal: " He then abandoned that pursuit and read Daoist books for his own pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: " He then gave up that pursuit and read Daoist texts for his own delight.

sentences.zh: 初訪道於牢山華蓋先生，久之出遊京師，因入建隆觀為道士。

translations.literal: At first he sought the Way from Master Huagai on Mount Lao; after a long while he traveled to the capital and entered Jianlong Abbey as a Daoist.
translations.idiomatic: He first studied the Way under Master Huagai on Mount Lao; later he went to the capital and entered Jianlong Abbey as a Daoist priest.

sentences.zh: 周曆四方。

translations.literal: He traveled all four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 以藥術濟人，不取其報。

translations.literal: He used medical arts to aid others and did not take payment.
translations.idiomatic: He treated people with medicine and never took payment.

sentences.zh: 祥符中，寓居晉州，性和靜無所好惡，晉人愛之。

translations.literal: During Xiangfu he lodged in Jin Prefecture; his nature was mild and still, without likes or dislikes, and the people of Jin loved him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiangfu era he lived in Jin Prefecture; gentle and even-tempered, he was beloved by the people there.

sentences.zh: 以為紫極宮主。

translations.literal: They made him abbot of the Purple Pole Palace.
translations.idiomatic: They made him abbot of the Purple Pole Palace.

sentences.zh: 年七十有五，遇人，或以為許元陽，語之曰：“汝風神秀異，有如李筌。

translations.literal: At seventy-five he met someone thought to be Xu Yuanyang, who said to him, "Your bearing and spirit are outstanding, like Li Quan.
translations.idiomatic: At seventy-five he met a man believed to be Xu Yuanyang, who told him, "Your bearing is extraordinary, like that of Li Quan.

sentences.zh: 雖老矣，尚可仙也。

translations.literal: Though old, you may still attain immortality.
translations.idiomatic: Though you are old, you may still become an immortal.

sentences.zh: ”因授煉形養元之訣，且曰：“得道如反掌，第行之惟艱，汝勉之。

translations.literal: " He then transmitted the secret of refining the body and nurturing the origin, and said, "Attaining the Way is like turning the palm—but carrying it out is hard; strive at it.
translations.idiomatic: " He then taught him the secret of refining the body and nurturing the primordial essence, adding, "Attaining the Way is as easy as turning one's palm—but doing it is hard; apply yourself.

sentences.zh: ”棲真行之二三年，漸反童顏，攀高攝危，輕若飛舉。

translations.literal: " Qizhen practiced for two or three years, gradually regaining a child's countenance; climbing heights and treading perilous places, he was light as if flying.
translations.idiomatic: " Qizhen practiced for two or three years, gradually regaining a youthful face; climbing heights and treading dangerous places, he moved as lightly as if he could fly.

sentences.zh: 乾興元年秋，謂其徒曰：“此歲之暮，吾當逝矣。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the first year of Qianxing he told his disciples, "At the end of this year I shall depart.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the first year of Qianxing (1022) he told his disciples, "At year's end I shall pass away.

sentences.zh: ”即宮西北隅自甃殯室。

translations.literal: " He then built his own burial chamber with bricks in the northwest corner of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: " He then built his own burial chamber of brick in the northwest corner of the palace.

sentences.zh: 室成，不食一月，與平居所知敘別，以十二月二日衣紙衣臥磚塌卒。

translations.literal: When the chamber was finished he ate nothing for a month, took leave of those he knew in ordinary life, and on the second day of the twelfth month, clad in paper garments, lay down on a brick couch and died.
translations.idiomatic: When it was finished he fasted for a month, bade farewell to his acquaintances, and on the second day of the twelfth month, dressed in paper garments, lay down on a brick couch and died.

sentences.zh: 人未之奇也。

translations.literal: People did not yet regard this as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: No one yet thought this remarkable.

sentences.zh: 及歲久，形如生，眾始驚，傳以為屍解。

translations.literal: After years passed his form was still as in life; the crowd was startled and spread word that he had achieved corpse liberation.
translations.idiomatic: Years later his body still looked alive; people were astonished and said he had achieved corpse liberation.

sentences.zh: 棲真自號神光子，與隱人海蟾子者以詩往還。

translations.literal: Qizhen styled himself Divine Radiance Master and exchanged poems with the recluse called Sea Toad Master.
translations.idiomatic: Qizhen styled himself Divine Radiance Master and exchanged poems with the recluse known as Sea Toad Master.

sentences.zh: 論養生秘術，目曰《還金篇》，凡兩卷。

translations.literal: Discussing secret arts of nurturing life, he entitled the work "Returning Gold," two fascicles in all.
translations.idiomatic: On secret arts of nurturing life he wrote Returning Gold in two fascicles.

sentences.zh: 楚衍，開封阼城人。

translations.literal: Chu Yan was a native of Zuocheng in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yan came from Zuocheng in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 少通四聲字母，裏人柳曜師事衍，裏中以先生目之。

translations.literal: In youth he mastered the four-tone initials; his fellow townsman Liu Yao studied under Yan, and the neighborhood called him Master.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he mastered the four-tone initials; his neighbor Liu Yao became his student, and locals addressed him as Master.

sentences.zh: 衍於《九章》、《緝古》、《綴術》、《海島》諸算經尤得其妙。

translations.literal: Yan especially grasped the subtleties of the mathematical classics Nine Chapters, Continuation of Ancient Mathematics, Continuation of Methods, and Sea Island.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had a particular mastery of the Nine Chapters, Continuation of Ancient Mathematics, Continuation of Methods, and Sea Island.

sentences.zh: 明相法及《聿斯經》，善推步、陰陽、星曆之數，間語休咎無不中。

translations.literal: He understood physiognomy and the Yusi Sutra, was skilled in calendrical calculation, yin-yang, and star almanacs; when he spoke of fortune and misfortune he never missed.
translations.idiomatic: He knew physiognomy and the Yusi Sutra, excelled in calendrical, yin-yang, and astronomical computation, and his predictions of fortune and misfortune never failed.

sentences.zh: 自陳試《宣明曆》，補司天監學生，遷保章正。

translations.literal: He presented himself to test the Xuanming Calendar, was appointed a student of the Directorate of Astronomy, and was promoted to Director of the Imperial Observatory.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted himself to examination on the Xuanming Calendar, entered the Directorate of Astronomy as a student, and rose to Director of the Imperial Observatory.

sentences.zh: 天聖初，造新曆，眾推衍明曆數，授靈台郎，與掌曆官宋行古等九人製崇天曆。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiansheng a new calendar was devised; the multitude recommended Yan for his mastery of calendrical numbers. He was appointed Astrological Officer and, with nine calendar officials including Song Xinggu, compiled the Chongtian Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tiansheng era (1023) a new calendar was commissioned; Yan was recognized for his calendrical skill, appointed Astrological Officer, and with Song Xinggu and seven others compiled the Chongtian Calendar.

sentences.zh: 進司天監丞，入隸翰林天文。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Directorate of Astronomy and entered the Hanlin as an astronomer.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Directorate of Astronomy and joined the Hanlin as an astronomer.

sentences.zh: 皇祐中，同造《司辰星漏曆》十二卷。

translations.literal: During Huangyou he jointly compiled the twelve-fascicle Calendar of the Office of Hours, Stars, and Clepsydra.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huangyou era (1049–1054) he helped compile the twelve-fascicle Calendar of the Office of Hours, Stars, and Clepsydra.

sentences.zh: 久之，與周琮同管勾司天監。

translations.literal: After a long while he and Zhou Cong jointly supervised the Directorate of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: Later he and Zhou Cong jointly supervised the Directorate of Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 卒，無子，有女亦善算術。

translations.literal: He died without sons; he had a daughter who was also skilled in calculation.
translations.idiomatic: He died childless; his daughter was also skilled in mathematics.

sentences.zh: 僧誌言，自言姓許，壽春人。

translations.literal: The monk Zhiyan said his surname was Xu and that he was from Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Zhiyan said his surname was Xu and that he came from Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 落發東京景德寺七俱胝院，事清遂。

translations.literal: He tonsured at the Seven Cundi Cloister of Jingde Temple in the Eastern Capital and served Qing Sui.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordained at the Seven Cundi Cloister of Jingde Temple in the Eastern Capital and studied under Qing Sui.

sentences.zh: 初，遂誦經勤苦，誌言忽造遂，跪前願為弟子。

translations.literal: At first Sui chanted sutras with bitter diligence; Zhiyan suddenly came to him, knelt before him, and asked to become his disciple.
translations.idiomatic: Sui at first chanted sutras with great diligence; Zhiyan suddenly appeared before him, knelt, and asked to become his disciple.

sentences.zh: 遂見其相貌奇古，直視不瞬，心異之，為授具戒。

translations.literal: Sui saw that his appearance was strangely archaic and that he stared straight ahead without blinking; his heart was struck, and he gave him full ordination.
translations.idiomatic: Sui saw his strangely archaic features and unblinking stare, was astonished, and gave him full ordination.

sentences.zh: 然動止軒昂，語笑無度，多行市裏，褰裳疾趨，舉指書空，佇立良久；

translations.literal: Yet his movements were lofty, his speech and laughter unbounded; he often walked the markets, hitching up his robe and hurrying, pointing at the sky and standing long in place;
translations.idiomatic: Yet his bearing was lofty and his laughter unrestrained; he often walked the markets with robes hitched up, hurrying along, pointing at the sky and standing motionless for long stretches;

sentences.zh: 時從屠酤遊，飲啖無所擇。

translations.literal: at times he consorted with butchers and wine sellers and ate and drank without discrimination.
translations.idiomatic: and he sometimes kept company with butchers and wine sellers, eating and drinking whatever came to hand.

sentences.zh: 眾以為狂，遂獨曰：“此異人也。

translations.literal: The crowd thought him mad, but Sui alone said, "This is an extraordinary man.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone thought him mad, but Sui alone said, "This is no ordinary man.

sentences.zh: 人有欲為齋施，輒先知其至，不召款門，指名取供。

translations.literal: When someone wished to offer a vegetarian feast, he always knew beforehand that they were coming; without being summoned he would open the door and call out names to take provisions.
translations.idiomatic: When someone planned a vegetarian offering, he always knew they were coming; without being summoned he would open the door and call out names to take what was needed.

sentences.zh: 溫州人林仲方自其家以摩衲來獻，舟始及岸，遽來取去。

translations.literal: Lin Zhongfang of Wenzhou was bringing a patched robe from his home as an offering; the boat had only just reached shore when Zhiyan came at once to take it away.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Zhongfang of Wenzhou was bringing a patched robe from home as an offering; the moment his boat touched shore, Zhiyan came and took it.

sentences.zh: 仁宗每延入禁中，徑登坐結趺，飯畢遽出，未嚐揖也。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong often invited him into the inner palace; he would go straight in, sit cross-legged, and leave as soon as he had eaten, never once bowing.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong often invited him into the inner palace; he would walk straight in, sit cross-legged, leave as soon as he had eaten, and never once bowed.

sentences.zh: 王公士庶召即赴，然莫與交一言者。

translations.literal: Princes, officials, and commoners summoned him and he would come, yet no one ever exchanged a word with him.
translations.idiomatic: Princes, officials, and commoners could summon him and he would come, yet no one ever got a word from him.

sentences.zh: 或陰卜休咎，書紙揮翰甚疾，字體遒壯，初不可曉，其後多驗。

translations.literal: At times he would secretly divine fortune and misfortune, writing on paper with very swift brushwork; the characters were forceful and strong, at first unintelligible, but afterward mostly proved true.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he would secretly divine fortune and misfortune, writing with swift, vigorous strokes that were at first unintelligible but later proved true.

sentences.zh: 仁宗春秋漸高，嗣未立，默遣內侍至言所。

translations.literal: As Renzong grew older and the heir was still unsettled, he quietly sent a palace attendant to Zhiyan's dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: As Renzong advanced in years without an heir named, he quietly sent a palace attendant to Zhiyan's dwelling.

sentences.zh: 言所書有“十三郎”字，人莫測何謂。

translations.literal: Among what Zhiyan wrote were the characters "Thirteenth Son"; no one could fathom what it meant.
translations.idiomatic: Among Zhiyan's writings were the characters "Thirteenth Son," which no one could interpret.

sentences.zh: 後英宗以濮王第十三子入繼，眾始悟。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Yingzong entered the succession as the thirteenth son of the Prince of Pu, and the multitude at last understood.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Yingzong succeeded as the thirteenth son of the Prince of Pu, and people at last understood.

sentences.zh: 大宗正守節請書，言不顧，迫之，得“潤州”字。

translations.literal: The Director of the Imperial Clan Shoujie asked for a writing; Zhiyan paid no heed, but when pressed he produced the characters "Run Prefecture."
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Imperial Clan Shoujie asked for a prophecy; Zhiyan ignored him, but when pressed wrote the characters "Run Prefecture."

sentences.zh: 未幾，守節薨，贈丹陽郡王。

translations.literal: Before long Shoujie died and was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Shoujie died and was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 見寺童義懷，撫其背曰：“德山、臨濟。

translations.literal: Seeing the temple boy Yi Huai, he stroked his back and said, "Deshan, Linji.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the temple boy Yi Huai, he stroked his back and said, "Deshan, Linji.

sentences.zh: ”懷既落發，住天衣，說法，大為學者所宗，其前知多類此。

translations.literal: " After Huai was ordained he resided at Tianyi and expounded the Dharma, greatly revered by scholars; his foreknowledge was mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: " After Huai was ordained he lived at Tianyi, taught the Dharma, and became greatly revered; most of Zhiyan's prophecies were of this sort.

sentences.zh: 普淨院施浴，夜漏初盡，門扉未啟，方迎佛而浴室有人聲，往視，則言在焉。

translations.literal: At Universal Purity Cloister a bathing charity was held; the night watch had just ended and the gates were not yet open—they were welcoming the Buddha when sounds came from the bathhouse; going to look, they found Zhiyan there.
translations.idiomatic: At Universal Purity Cloister a communal bathing was held; the night watch had just ended and the gates were still closed—they were welcoming the Buddha when voices came from the bathhouse; they looked in and found Zhiyan there.

sentences.zh: 有具齋薦鱠者，並食之，臨流而吐，化為小鮮，群泳而去。

translations.literal: Someone had prepared a vegetarian feast with sliced fish; he ate it all, then spat by the stream and it turned into small fish that swam away in a school.
translations.idiomatic: Someone had prepared a vegetarian feast with sliced fish; he ate it all, then spat into the stream and it turned into small fish that swam away in a school.

sentences.zh: 海客遇風且沒，見僧操縆引舶而濟。

translations.literal: A seafarer caught in wind and about to sink saw a monk handling a rope and drawing the boat to safety.
translations.idiomatic: A seafarer caught in a storm and about to sink saw a monk hauling on a rope and towing his boat to safety.

sentences.zh: 客至都下遇言，忽謂之曰：“非我，汝奈何？

translations.literal: When the traveler reached the capital and met Zhiyan, he suddenly said to him, "If not for me, what would you have done?
translations.idiomatic: When the traveler reached the capital and met Zhiyan, Zhiyan suddenly said, "Without me, what would you have done?

sentences.zh: ”客記其貌，真引舟者也。

translations.literal: " The traveler noted his appearance—it was truly the one who had towed the boat.
translations.idiomatic: " The traveler noted his face: he was indeed the monk who had towed the boat.

sentences.zh: 與曹州士趙棠善，後棠棄官隱居番禺。

translations.literal: He was on good terms with Zhao Tang, a gentleman of Cao Prefecture; later Tang abandoned office and lived in seclusion at Panyu.
translations.idiomatic: He was friends with Zhao Tang, a scholar of Cao Prefecture; later Tang resigned his office and lived in seclusion at Panyu.

sentences.zh: 人傳棠與言數以偈頌相寄，萬里間輒數日而達。

translations.literal: People reported that Tang and Zhiyan often sent each other gatha and hymns; across ten thousand li they arrived within a few days.
translations.idiomatic: People said Tang and Zhiyan often exchanged verses across thousands of miles, which arrived within a few days.

sentences.zh: 棠死，亦盛夏身不壞。

translations.literal: When Tang died, even in midsummer his body did not decay.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang died, even in midsummer his body did not decay.

sentences.zh: 言將死，作頌，不可曉。

translations.literal: As Zhiyan was about to die he composed a hymn that could not be understood.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhiyan was about to die he composed a hymn that no one could understand.

sentences.zh: 已而曰：“我從古始成就，逃多國土，今南國矣。

translations.literal: Then he said, "From antiquity I have achieved completion, fled many lands, and now it is the southern realm.
translations.idiomatic: Then he said, "Since antiquity I have achieved completion, fled many lands, and now it is the southern realm.

sentences.zh: ”仁宗遣內侍以真身塑像置寺中，榜曰顯化禪師。

translations.literal: " Renzong sent a palace attendant to place a true-body image in the temple and bestowed the plaque Manifest Transformation Chan Master.
translations.idiomatic: " Renzong sent a palace attendant to place a true-body image in the temple and gave him the posthumous title Manifest Transformation Chan Master.

sentences.zh: 其後善厚者禮之，見額上熒然有光，就視之，得舍利。

translations.literal: Afterward those who devoutly honored him saw a gleaming light on his forehead; drawing near to look, they obtained a relic.
translations.idiomatic: Later those who honored him devoutly saw a gleaming light on his forehead; when they looked closely, they found a relic.

sentences.zh: 僧懷丙，真定人。

translations.literal: The monk Huaibing was a man of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Huaibing was a native of Zhending.

sentences.zh: 巧思出天性，非學所能至也。

translations.literal: Ingenious designs issued from his inborn nature; it was not something that learning could attain.
translations.idiomatic: His ingenuity came from inborn talent, not from anything learning could impart.

sentences.zh: 真定構木為浮圖十三級，勢尤孤絕。

translations.literal: At Zhending they had built a thirteen-tier wooden pagoda, its stance especially solitary and lofty.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhending stood a thirteen-story wooden pagoda, towering and solitary.

sentences.zh: 既久而中級大柱壞，欲西北傾，他匠莫能為。

translations.literal: After a long time the great pillar at the middle tier was damaged, and it was about to lean northwest; no other craftsmen could do anything about it.
translations.idiomatic: In time the great central pillar of the middle tier gave way, and the structure threatened to tilt northwest; no other craftsman could remedy it.

sentences.zh: 懷丙度短長，別作柱，命眾工維而上。

translations.literal: Huaibing measured lengths, fashioned a separate pillar, and ordered the workers to hold it up.
translations.idiomatic: Huaibing measured the dimensions, made a replacement pillar, and had the workmen hoist it into place.

sentences.zh: 已而卻眾工，以一介自從，閉戶良久，易柱下，不聞斧鑿聲。

translations.literal: Thereupon he dismissed the workers, taking only one attendant with him; he shut the door for a long while and replaced the pillar below, without the sound of ax or chisel being heard.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent the workmen away, keeping only a single attendant, shut himself in for a long while, and replaced the pillar without a sound of ax or chisel.

sentences.zh: 趙州洨河鑿石為橋，熔鐵貫其中。

translations.literal: At Zhaozhou on the Jiao River they quarried stone to make a bridge, melting iron to run through it.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhaozhou on the Jiao River a bridge was built of quarried stone with molten iron run through its joints.

sentences.zh: 自唐以來相傳數百年，大水不能壞。

translations.literal: From the Tang down it had been handed on for several hundred years; great floods could not destroy it.
translations.idiomatic: It had stood for centuries since the Tang, surviving even the fiercest floods.

sentences.zh: 歲久，鄉民多盜鑿鐵，橋遂欹倒，計千夫不能正。

translations.literal: As years passed, local people stole and chiseled out much iron; the bridge then toppled sideways, and it was estimated that a thousand men could not set it right.
translations.idiomatic: Over the years locals pilfered iron from it until the bridge collapsed; by one estimate even a thousand laborers could not set it right.

sentences.zh: 懷丙不役眾工，以術正之，使復故。

translations.literal: Huaibing did not employ masses of workers; by technique he set it right and restored it to its former state.
translations.idiomatic: Without mobilizing a large work force, Huaibing restored the bridge to its original condition by his own methods.

sentences.zh: 河中府浮梁用鐵牛八維之，一牛且數萬斤。

translations.literal: The floating bridge at Hezhong Prefecture was held by eight iron oxen; one ox weighed nearly ten thousand jin.
translations.idiomatic: The floating bridge at Hezhong Prefecture was anchored by eight iron oxen, each weighing nearly ten thousand jin.

sentences.zh: 後水暴漲絕梁，牽牛沒於河，募能出之者。

translations.literal: Later a sudden flood severed the bridge and dragged an ox under the river; they sought someone who could recover it.
translations.idiomatic: Later a sudden flood broke the bridge and dragged one of the oxen under the river; a reward was posted for anyone who could raise it.

sentences.zh: 懷丙以二大舟實土，夾牛維之，用大木為權衡狀鉤牛，徐去其土，舟浮牛出。

translations.literal: Huaibing filled two large boats with earth, placed them on either side of the ox and secured them to it, fashioned a large wooden lever shaped like a steelyard to hook the ox, and slowly removed the earth; the boats floated and the ox came out.
translations.idiomatic: Huaibing loaded two large boats with earth, moored them on either side of the ox, hooked the ox with a great wooden lever, and slowly unloaded the earth; as the boats rose, the ox came up with them.

sentences.zh: 轉運使張燾以聞，賜紫衣。

translations.literal: Transport Commissioner Zhang Tao reported it, and Huaibing was granted purple robes.
translations.idiomatic: Transport Commissioner Zhang Tao reported the feat to the throne, and Huaibing was awarded purple robes.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 許希，開封人。

translations.literal: Xu Xi was a man of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xi was a native of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 以醫為業，補翰林醫學。

translations.literal: He took medicine as his profession and was appointed Hanlin Medical Scholar.
translations.idiomatic: He practiced medicine and was appointed Hanlin Medical Scholar.

sentences.zh: 景祐元年，仁宗不豫，侍醫數進藥，不效，人心憂恐。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingyou, Emperor Renzong fell ill; the attending physicians repeatedly offered medicine without effect, and people's hearts were anxious and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Jingyou era, Emperor Renzong fell ill. The palace physicians prescribed medicine again and again to no effect, and dread spread through the court.

sentences.zh: 冀國大長公主薦希，希診曰：“針心下包絡之間，可亟愈。

translations.literal: The Elder Princess of the State of Ji recommended Xi; Xi examined him and said, "Needling between the pericardium beneath the heart will bring swift recovery.
translations.idiomatic: The Elder Princess of Ji recommended Xu Xi. On examining the emperor he said, "Needling the area between the pericardium and the lower heart will bring a swift cure.

sentences.zh: ”左右爭以為不可，諸黃門祈以身試，試之，無所害。

translations.literal: " Those at the emperor's side all contended it could not be done; the palace eunuchs begged to test it on themselves; when tested, there was no harm.
translations.idiomatic: " Those around the throne protested that this was impossible, but several eunuchs volunteered to be needled first; the treatment did them no harm.

sentences.zh: 遂以針進，而帝疾愈。

translations.literal: Thereupon he administered the needles, and the emperor's illness was cured.
translations.idiomatic: The needles were then applied to the emperor, and he recovered.

sentences.zh: 命為翰林醫官，賜緋衣、銀魚及器幣。

translations.literal: He was appointed Hanlin Medical Officer and granted scarlet robes, silver fish insignia, and vessels and silks.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Hanlin Medical Officer and given scarlet robes, a silver fish insignia, and gifts of vessels and silk.

sentences.zh: 希拜謝已，又西向拜，帝問其故，對曰：“扁鵲，臣師也。

translations.literal: After Xi had bowed in thanks, he bowed again facing west; the emperor asked the reason, and he replied, "Bian Que was my teacher.
translations.idiomatic: After accepting the honors, Xu Xi bowed again toward the west. When the emperor asked why, he replied, "Bian Que was my master.

sentences.zh: 今者非臣之功，殆臣師之賜，安敢忘師乎？

translations.literal: Today's outcome is not my achievement but rather my teacher's gift; how dare I forget my teacher?
translations.idiomatic: This cure is not my accomplishment but my master's gift—how could I forget him?

sentences.zh: ”乃請以所得金興扁鵲廟。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he requested to use the gold he had received to renovate Bian Que's temple.
translations.idiomatic: " He asked that the gold he had received be used to restore the temple of Bian Que.

sentences.zh: 帝為築廟於城西隅，封靈應侯。

translations.literal: The emperor had a temple built for him at the city's western corner and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Spiritual Response.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor built the temple in the western quarter of the city and ennobled Bian Que as Marquis of Spiritual Responsiveness.

sentences.zh: 其後廟益完，學醫者歸趨之，因立太醫局於其旁。

translations.literal: Afterward the temple grew ever more complete; students of medicine flocked to it, and consequently the Imperial Medical Bureau was established beside it.
translations.idiomatic: The temple grew more splendid over time, medical students flocked there, and the Imperial Medical Bureau was eventually established beside it.

sentences.zh: 希至殿中省尚藥奉禦，卒。

translations.literal: Xi rose to Imperial Pharmacy Attendant in the Palace Domestic Service, then died.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xi rose to the post of Imperial Pharmacy Attendant in the Palace Domestic Service and later died.

sentences.zh: 著《神應針經要訣》行於世。

translations.literal: He authored Essentials of the Divine Response Acupuncture Canon, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Essentials of the Divine Response Acupuncture Canon, which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 錄其子宗道至內殿崇班。

translations.literal: His son Zongdao was enrolled in the Inner Hall Honored Company.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zongdao was granted appointment in the Inner Hall Honored Company.

sentences.zh: 龐安時字安常，蘄州蘄水人。

translations.literal: Pang Anshi, style name Anchang, was a man of Qishui in Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Anshi, styled Anchang, was a native of Qishui in Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 兒時能讀書，過目輒記。

translations.literal: As a child he could read books; what passed before his eyes he memorized at once.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy he read with ease and remembered whatever he saw.

sentences.zh: 父，世醫也，授以脈訣。

translations.literal: His father was a hereditary physician and taught him pulse formulas.
translations.idiomatic: His father came from a family of physicians and taught him pulse diagnosis.

sentences.zh: 安時曰：“是不足為也。

translations.literal: Anshi said, "This is not worth doing.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi said, "That is hardly worth pursuing.

sentences.zh: ”獨取黃帝、扁鵲之脈書治之，未久，已能通其說，時出新意，辨詰不可屈，父大驚，時年猶未冠。

translations.literal: " He alone took the pulse books of the Yellow Emperor and Bian Que and studied them; before long he could master their doctrines, constantly producing new ideas; in disputation none could overcome him; his father was greatly astonished—he was not yet capped.
translations.idiomatic: " He turned instead to the pulse classics attributed to the Yellow Emperor and Bian Que. Before long he had mastered them, constantly innovating, and in debate no one could best him. His father was astonished—Anshi was not yet twenty.

sentences.zh: 已而病聵，乃益讀《靈樞》、《太素》、《甲乙》諸秘書，凡經傳百家之涉其道者，靡不通貫。

translations.literal: Thereafter he fell ill with deafness; he then read ever more the Secret Books—the Spiritual Pivot, the Great Plain, the A-B—and whatever in the classics and the hundred schools touched upon the Way, none did he fail to master thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: When he later went deaf, he threw himself into the medical canon—the Spiritual Pivot, the Great Plain, the A-B Canon—and every classic or treatise that touched on medicine until he had mastered them all.

sentences.zh: 嚐曰：“世所謂醫書，予皆見之，惟扁鵲之言深矣。

translations.literal: He once said, "Of what the world calls medical books, I have seen them all; only Bian Que's words are profound.
translations.idiomatic: He once remarked, "I have read every medical book the world knows; only Bian Que's teaching runs deepest.

sentences.zh: 蓋所謂《難經》者，扁鵲寓術於其書，而言之不祥，意者使後人自求之歟！

translations.literal: Presumably the so-called Classic of Difficult Issues is a book in which Bian Que lodged his art, yet spoke in veiled terms—perhaps meaning that later people should seek it out for themselves!
translations.idiomatic: The so-called Classic of Difficult Issues embeds Bian Que's art in cryptic language, as if inviting later generations to discover its meaning for themselves.

sentences.zh: 予之術蓋出於此。

translations.literal: My art presumably issues from this.
translations.idiomatic: My own practice derives from this source.

sentences.zh: 以之視淺深，決死生，若合符節。

translations.literal: Using it to discern shallow and deep, to decide life and death—it was like fitting tally halves together.
translations.idiomatic: With it I gauge the depth of disease and judge life and death as surely as matching tally halves.

sentences.zh: 且察脈之要，莫急於人迎、寸口。

translations.literal: Moreover, in examining pulses, nothing is more urgent than the human welcome and the inch opening.
translations.idiomatic: Of pulse diagnosis, nothing matters more than the carotid artery and the wrist pulse at the inch opening.

sentences.zh: 是二脈陰陽相應，如兩引繩，陰陽均，則繩之大小等，故定陰陽於喉、手，配覆溢於尺、寸，寓九候於浮沉，分四溫於傷寒。

translations.literal: These two pulses respond to yin and yang like two ropes being pulled; when yin and yang are balanced, the ropes are equal in size; thus he fixed yin and yang at the throat and hand, paired overflow and deficiency at the foot and inch positions, lodged the nine indicators in floating and sinking, and divided the four warmths in cold damage.
translations.idiomatic: These two pulses mirror yin and yang like paired ropes of equal tension. I therefore anchor yin and yang at the throat and wrist, match overflow and deficiency at the foot and inch positions, read the nine pulse signs in floating and sinking, and distinguish the four stages of cold-damage fever.

sentences.zh: 此皆扁鵲略開其端，而予參以《內經》諸書，考究而得其說。

translations.literal: All this Bian Que had slightly opened at the start, and I collated it with the books of the Inner Canon, investigating until I grasped the doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Que merely opened these paths; I reconciled them with the Inner Canon and worked out the full doctrine.

sentences.zh: 審而用之，順而治之，病不得逃矣。

translations.literal: Examining and applying it, treating in accord with it—illness cannot escape.
translations.idiomatic: Applied with care and treatment aligned to it, no illness can escape.

sentences.zh: ”又欲以術告後世，故著《難經辨》數萬言。

translations.literal: " He also wished to transmit his art to later generations, and therefore authored Discourse on the Classic of Difficult Issues in tens of thousands of words.
translations.idiomatic: " Wishing to pass his art to posterity, he also wrote Discourse on the Classic of Difficult Issues, running to tens of thousands of words.

sentences.zh: 觀草木之性與五藏之宜，秩其職任，官其寒熱，班其奇偶，以療百疾，著《主對集》一卷。

translations.literal: Observing the natures of plants and what suited the five viscera, ranking their duties, assigning their cold and heat, arranging their odd and even pairings to treat a hundred diseases, he authored Collection of Principal Pairings in one fascicle.
translations.idiomatic: He observed how herbs suited the five viscera, ranked their roles, matched cold and heat properties, and arranged odd-even pairings to treat every ailment, writing Collection of Principal Pairings in one volume.

sentences.zh: 古今異宜，方術脫遺，備陰陽之變，補仲景《論》。

translations.literal: Ancient and modern differ in what is suitable; formulas and techniques had been lost; he supplied the transformations of yin and yang and supplemented Zhang Zhongjing's Treatise.
translations.idiomatic: Because ancient and modern conditions differ and formulas had been lost, he supplied treatments for yin-yang transformations and supplemented Zhang Zhongjing's Treatise on Cold Damage.

sentences.zh: 藥有後出，古所未知，今不能辨，嚐試有功，不可遺也。

translations.literal: Some drugs had appeared later, unknown to antiquity; though not yet fully distinguished today, trial had shown them effective—they must not be omitted.
translations.idiomatic: Some medicines were of recent discovery, unknown to antiquity; though not yet fully classified, trials proved them effective and deserved inclusion.

sentences.zh: 作《本草補遺》。

translations.literal: He produced Supplement to the Materia Medica.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Supplement to the Materia Medica.

sentences.zh: 為人治病，率十愈八九。

translations.literal: When treating people's illnesses, roughly nine or ten out of ten recovered.
translations.idiomatic: In treating patients he cured roughly eight or nine cases out of ten.

sentences.zh: 踵門求診者，為辟邸舍居之，親視饘粥、藥物，必愈而後遣；

translations.literal: Those who came to his door seeking consultation—he would set aside lodging for them to stay, personally overseeing their gruel, medicine, and herbs; only after recovery would he send them away;
translations.idiomatic: For patients who came to his door he set aside quarters, personally attending to their meals and medicines, and sent them away only after they recovered;

sentences.zh: 其不可為者，必實告之，不復為治。

translations.literal: For those who could not be treated, he always told them plainly and would not treat them further.
translations.idiomatic: when a case was hopeless he told them plainly and refused further treatment.

sentences.zh: 活人無數。

translations.literal: He saved countless lives.
translations.idiomatic: He saved countless lives.

sentences.zh: 病家持金帛來謝，不盡取也。

translations.literal: When families brought gold and silk to thank him, he did not take it all.
translations.idiomatic: When grateful families brought gold and silk, he never took all they offered.

sentences.zh: 嚐詣舒之桐城，有民家婦孕將產，七日而子不下，百術無所效。

translations.literal: He once went to Tongcheng in Shu; a commoner's wife was pregnant and about to deliver; for seven days the child would not descend, and a hundred methods had no effect.
translations.idiomatic: Once in Tongcheng, Shu, he was called to a pregnant woman who had labored for seven days without delivering; every remedy had failed.

sentences.zh: 安時之弟子李百全適在傍舍，邀安時往視之。

translations.literal: Anshi's disciple Li Baiquan happened to be in a neighboring house and invited Anshi to go examine her.
translations.idiomatic: His disciple Li Baiquan happened to be nearby and summoned Anshi to examine her.

sentences.zh: 才見，即連呼不死，令其家人以湯溫其腰腹，自為上下拊摩。

translations.literal: As soon as he saw her, he repeatedly cried that she would not die, ordered her family to warm her waist and belly with hot water, and himself massaged up and down.
translations.idiomatic: At first sight he cried repeatedly, "She will not die!" He had her family apply warm compresses to her waist and belly and massaged her abdomen himself.

sentences.zh: 孕者覺腸胃微痛，呻吟間生一男子。

translations.literal: The pregnant woman felt slight pain in her intestines and stomach; amid groaning she gave birth to a boy.
translations.idiomatic: The woman felt a slight cramp in her abdomen and, with a moan, delivered a boy.

sentences.zh: 其家驚喜，而不知所以然。

translations.literal: Her family was startled and delighted, yet did not know why it happened.
translations.idiomatic: The family was astonished and overjoyed but did not understand how it had happened.

sentences.zh: 安時曰：“兒已出胞，而一手誤執母腸不復能脫，故非符藥所能為。

translations.literal: Anshi said, "The child had already left the womb, but one hand had mistakenly grasped the mother's intestines and could not be released; therefore no formula-medicine could accomplish it.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi explained, "The infant had left the womb, but one hand had caught the mother's intestines and would not release—no herbal formula could solve that.

sentences.zh: 吾隔腹捫兒手所在，針其虎口，既痛即縮手，所以遽生，無他術也。

translations.literal: I felt through the belly where the child's hand lay and needled the tiger's mouth point; once it hurt, the hand withdrew—that is why birth came so swiftly; there was no other technique.
translations.idiomatic: I palpated through the abdomen to find the hand and needled the Hegu point on the tiger's mouth. Pain made the hand withdraw—that is why delivery came so suddenly. Nothing more was involved.

sentences.zh: ”取兒視之，右手虎口針痕存焉。

translations.literal: " They took the child to look—on the right hand at the tiger's mouth the needle mark remained.
translations.idiomatic: " When they examined the infant, the needle mark remained on the tiger's mouth of his right hand.

sentences.zh: 其妙如此。

translations.literal: His skill was such as this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the marvel of his art.

sentences.zh: 有問以華佗之事者，曰：“術若是，非人所能為也。

translations.literal: When someone asked about Hua Tuo's deeds, he said, "If the art were like that, it is not something a human could do.
translations.idiomatic: When asked about the stories of Hua Tuo, he said, "Art like that is beyond human capacity.

sentences.zh: 其史之妄乎！

translations.literal: Are they not the historians' fabrications!
translations.idiomatic: Surely the historians invented them!

sentences.zh: ”年五十八而疾作，門人請自視脈，笑曰：“吾察之審矣。

translations.literal: " At age fifty-eight his illness arose; disciples asked him to examine his own pulse; he laughed and said, "I have examined it carefully.
translations.idiomatic: " At fifty-eight he fell ill. When disciples asked to take his pulse, he smiled and said, "I have already examined it thoroughly.

sentences.zh: 且出入息亦脈也，今胃氣已絕。

translations.literal: Moreover, the rise and fall of breath is also a pulse; now stomach qi is already exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Even the rhythm of breath is a kind of pulse, and my stomach qi is already gone.

sentences.zh: 死矣。

translations.literal: I am dead.
translations.idiomatic: I am as good as dead.

sentences.zh: ”遂屏卻藥餌。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he put aside medicine.
translations.idiomatic: " He then refused all medicine.

sentences.zh: 後數日，與客坐語而卒。

translations.literal: Several days later, while sitting conversing with a guest, he died.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later he died conversing with a guest.

sentences.zh: 錢乙字仲陽，本吳越王俶支屬，祖從北遷，遂為鄆州人。

translations.literal: Qian Yi, style name Zhongyang, was originally a collateral of King Qian Chu of Wuyue; his grandfather followed the northward migration and thus became a man of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Yi, styled Zhongyang, was descended from a collateral branch of King Qian Chu of Wuyue; his grandfather moved north with the court and settled in Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 父穎善醫，然嗜酒喜遊，一旦，東之海上不反。

translations.literal: His father Ying was skilled in medicine, yet loved wine and delighted in wandering; one day he went east to the sea and did not return.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ying was a skilled physician but fond of wine and travel; one day he sailed east to the sea and never returned.

sentences.zh: 乙方三歲，母前死，姑嫁呂氏，哀而收養之，長誨之醫，乃告以家世。

translations.literal: When Yi was three, his mother had already died; his aunt, married to the Lu family, took pity and adopted him; as he grew she instructed him in medicine and then told him of the family history.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was three when his mother died. His aunt, married into the Lu family, took pity on him and raised him, teaching him medicine as he grew and finally revealing their family history.

sentences.zh: 即泣，請往跡尋，凡八九反。

translations.literal: He wept at once and begged to go trace and search; altogether eight or nine times.
translations.idiomatic: He wept and begged to search for his father, making the journey eight or nine times.

sentences.zh: 積數歲，遂迎父以歸，時已三十年矣。

translations.literal: Over several years he finally welcomed his father home; thirty years had already passed.
translations.idiomatic: After several years he finally brought his father home—thirty years after he had vanished.

sentences.zh: 鄉人感慨，賦詩詠之。

translations.literal: The villagers were moved and composed poems praising this.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by the tale, neighbors composed poems in praise.

sentences.zh: 其事呂如事父，呂沒無嗣，為收葬行服。

translations.literal: He served the Lu family as he would a father; when Lu died without heirs, he performed burial and mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: He honored the Lu family as he would his own father; when his foster father died childless, Yi buried him and observed full mourning.

sentences.zh: 乙始以《顱

translations.literal: Yi first, through the Cranial
translations.idiomatic: Yi first won renown for his Cranial

sentences.zh: (囟頁）

translations.literal: (fontanel + page)
translations.idiomatic: (fontanel + page)

sentences.zh: 方》著名，至京師視長公主女疾，授翰林醫學。

translations.literal: Formula, became famous; he went to the capital to treat the Elder Grand Princess's daughter's illness and was appointed Hanlin Medical Scholar.
translations.idiomatic: and Fontanel Formula; he came to the capital to treat the Elder Grand Princess's daughter and was appointed Hanlin Medical Scholar.

sentences.zh: 皇子病瘈疭，乙進黃土湯而愈。

translations.literal: The imperial prince fell ill with convulsions; Yi administered yellow-earth decoction and he recovered.
translations.idiomatic: When a prince suffered convulsions, Yi cured him with a decoction of yellow earth.

sentences.zh: 神宗召問黃土所以愈疾狀，對曰：“以土勝水，水得其平，則風自止。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong summoned him and asked why yellow earth could cure the illness; he replied, "Earth overcomes water; when water is balanced, wind naturally stops.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong asked why yellow earth had cured the illness. Yi replied, "Earth restrains water; when water is balanced, wind ceases of itself.

sentences.zh: ”帝悅，擢太醫丞，賜金紫。

translations.literal: " The emperor was pleased, promoted him to Vice Director of the Imperial Medical Service, and granted gold and purple robes.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was pleased, promoted him to Vice Director of the Imperial Medical Service, and bestowed gold and purple robes.

sentences.zh: 由是公卿宗戚家延致無虛日。

translations.literal: From this the households of high officials and imperial kin invited him without an idle day.
translations.idiomatic: From then on grandees and imperial kinsmen vied to summon him every day.

sentences.zh: 廣親宗子病，診之曰：“此可毋藥而愈。

translations.literal: A clansman of the Extended Kindred fell ill; examining him Yi said, "This can be cured without medicine.
translations.idiomatic: A clansman of the Extended Kindred fell ill. Yi examined him and said, "This needs no medicine to cure.

sentences.zh: ”其幼在傍，指之曰：“是且暴疾驚人，後三日過午，可無恙。

translations.literal: " A young child stood beside; pointing to him he said, "This one is about to suffer a sudden illness that will frighten people; after three days past noon, he will be unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: " A young child stood nearby. Pointing at him, Yi said, "That child will soon suffer a sudden seizure that will terrify everyone, but after noon on the third day he will be fine.

sentences.zh: ”其家恚，不答。

translations.literal: " The family was angry and gave no reply.
translations.idiomatic: " The family took offense and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 明日，幼果發{疒間}甚急，召乙治之，三日愈。

translations.literal: The next day, the child indeed suffered a convulsive disorder with great urgency; they summoned Yi to treat him, and in three days he recovered.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the child did suffer a violent epileptic fit. They summoned Yi, and within three days the child recovered.

sentences.zh: 問其故，曰：“火色直視，心與肝俱受邪。

translations.literal: When asked the reason, he said, "Fire color with straight staring—the heart and liver were both affected by pathogen.
translations.idiomatic: When asked to explain, he said, "His eyes showed fire-red staring—both heart and liver were afflicted.

sentences.zh: 過午者，所用時當更也。

translations.literal: Passing noon means the active time-cycle ought to change.
translations.idiomatic: After noon the governing time-cycle would shift.

sentences.zh: ”王子病嘔泄，他醫與剛劑，加喘焉。

translations.literal: " A prince fell ill with vomiting and diarrhea; other physicians gave strong formulas, and wheezing was added.
translations.idiomatic: " A prince suffered vomiting and diarrhea. Other physicians prescribed strong formulas, and wheezing developed.

sentences.zh: 乙曰：“是本中熱，脾且傷，奈何復燥之？

translations.literal: Yi said, "The root is interior heat; the spleen is already injured—why dry it further?
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "The root problem is interior heat and the spleen is already damaged—why apply drying medicines?

sentences.zh: 將不得前後溲。

translations.literal: Soon he will be unable to urinate or defecate.
translations.idiomatic: He will soon lose control of urination and defecation.

sentences.zh: ”與之石膏湯，王不信，謝去。

translations.literal: " He gave him gypsum decoction; the prince did not believe and took leave.
translations.idiomatic: " He offered gypsum decoction, but the prince refused to believe him and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 信宿浸劇，竟如言而效。

translations.literal: After one night and two days the illness grew severe; in the end it turned out as he had said and the treatment worked.
translations.idiomatic: Two nights later the illness worsened exactly as he had warned; when they finally used his remedy, it worked.

sentences.zh: 士病欬，麵青而光，氣哽哽。

translations.literal: A gentleman fell ill with cough; his face was bluish and shiny, his breath choked and gasping.
translations.idiomatic: A scholar suffered a cough, his face bluish and shining, his breath choked and labored.

sentences.zh: 乙曰：“肝乘肺，此逆候也。

translations.literal: Yi said, "The liver is overbearing upon the lung—this is a rebellious sign.
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "The liver is overwhelming the lung—a grave inverse pattern.

sentences.zh: 若秋得之，可治；

translations.literal: If obtained in autumn, it can be treated;
translations.idiomatic: Had this arisen in autumn, it could be treated;

sentences.zh: 今春，不可治。

translations.literal: Now in spring, it cannot be treated.
translations.idiomatic: but in spring it cannot be cured.

sentences.zh: ”其人祈哀，強予藥。

translations.literal: " The man begged piteously; Yi was compelled to give medicine.
translations.idiomatic: " The man pleaded desperately, and Yi reluctantly prescribed medicine.

sentences.zh: 明日，曰：“吾藥再瀉肝，而不少卻；

translations.literal: The next day he said, "My medicine purged the liver twice, yet did not recede in the least;
translations.idiomatic: The next day he said, "My medicine has purged the liver twice, yet the illness has not abated in the least;

sentences.zh: 三補肺，而益虛；

translations.literal: Thrice it tonified the lung, yet the deficiency grew worse;
translations.idiomatic: Three times it tonified the lung, yet his weakness only grew worse;

sentences.zh: 又加唇白，法當三日死。

translations.literal: Moreover his lips turned white; by rule he ought to die within three days.
translations.idiomatic: His lips have also turned pale; by medical rule he should die within three days.

sentences.zh: 今尚能粥，當過期。

translations.literal: Now he can still take gruel; he ought to pass the deadline.
translations.idiomatic: Since he can still take gruel, he may survive past the deadline.

sentences.zh: ”居五日而絕。

translations.literal: " After five days he died.
translations.idiomatic: " Five days later he died.

sentences.zh: 孕婦病，醫言胎且墜。

translations.literal: A pregnant woman fell ill; physicians said the fetus would miscarry.
translations.idiomatic: A pregnant woman fell ill; physicians said she would miscarry.

sentences.zh: 乙曰：“娠者五藏傳養，率六旬乃更。

translations.literal: Yi said, "In pregnancy the five viscera transmit nourishment in turn; roughly every sixty days they change.
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "During pregnancy the five viscera take turns nourishing the fetus, changing roughly every sixty days.

sentences.zh: 誠能候其月，偏補之，何必墜？

translations.literal: If one can truly await the proper month and supplement accordingly, why must there be miscarriage?
translations.idiomatic: If one can truly align treatment with the active month and tonify that organ specifically, why must the fetus be lost?

sentences.zh: ”已而母子皆得全。

translations.literal: " Subsequently both mother and child were preserved whole.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end both mother and child were saved.

sentences.zh: 又乳婦因悸而病，既愈，目張不得瞑。

translations.literal: Also a nursing woman fell ill from fright; after recovery her eyes stayed open and she could not close them.
translations.idiomatic: A nursing woman also fell ill from shock; though otherwise recovered, her eyes remained wide open and she could not sleep.

sentences.zh: 乙曰：“ 煮鬱李酒飲之使醉，即愈。

translations.literal: Yi said, " Boil bush-cherry wine and have her drink until drunk, and she will immediately recover.
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "Brew wine with bush cherry and have her drink until drunk—the cure will be immediate.

sentences.zh: 所以然者，目係內連肝膽，恐則氣結，膽衡不下。

translations.literal: The reason is that the eyes connect internally to liver and gallbladder; fear then binds qi, and the gallbladder's counterflow does not descend.
translations.idiomatic: The reason is that the eyes connect internally to the liver and gallbladder; fear binds the qi and keeps the gallbladder from descending.

sentences.zh: 鬱李能去結，隨酒入膽，結去膽下，則目能瞑矣。

translations.literal: Bush cherry can remove binding; following wine it enters the gallbladder; binding gone and gallbladder down, then the eyes can close.
translations.idiomatic: Bush cherry dispels binding; carried by wine into the gallbladder, it releases the knot so the gallbladder descends and the eyes can close again.

sentences.zh: ”飲之，果驗。

translations.literal: " She drank it, and it indeed proved true.
translations.idiomatic: " She drank as prescribed, and the cure worked exactly as he said.

sentences.zh: 乙本有羸疾，每自以意治之，而後甚，歎曰：“此所謂周痹也。

translations.literal: Yi originally had a wasting illness; he always treated it by his own judgment, and afterward it grew severe; he sighed and said, "This is what is called pervading numbness.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had long suffered a wasting illness and treated himself by his own judgment, but it only worsened. He sighed and said, "This is what is called pervasive numbness.

sentences.zh: 入藏者死，吾其已夫。

translations.literal: When it enters the viscera one dies—I am probably finished.
translations.idiomatic: If it enters the viscera, death follows—I suppose I am done for.

sentences.zh: ”既而曰：“吾能移之使在末。

translations.literal: " Then he said, "I can shift it to the extremities.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he said, "I can shift it to the extremities.

sentences.zh: ”因自製藥，日夜飲之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he compounded medicine himself and drank it day and night.
translations.idiomatic: " He then compounded his own medicine and drank it day and night.

sentences.zh: 左手足忽攣不能用，喜曰：“可矣！

translations.literal: His left hand and foot suddenly cramped and could not be used; he rejoiced and said, "It will do!
translations.idiomatic: His left hand and foot suddenly cramped and became useless. Delighted, he cried, "It worked!

sentences.zh: ”所親登東山，得茯苓大逾鬥。

translations.literal: " A close associate climbed Mount Dong and obtained a fu-ling larger than a peck measure.
translations.idiomatic: " A kinsman climbed Mount Dong and found a piece of fu-ling larger than a peck basket.

sentences.zh: 以法啖之盡，由是雖偏廢，而風骨悍堅如全人。

translations.literal: By the proper method he ate it all; from this, though partially disabled, his vigor and bone were fierce and firm like a whole man.
translations.idiomatic: He ate it all by the proper method; thereafter, though half-crippled, his physique remained as robust as a healthy man's.

sentences.zh: 以病免歸，不復出。

translations.literal: Due to illness he was dismissed and returned home, never coming out again.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned on grounds of illness and went home, never practicing again.

sentences.zh: 乙為方不名一師，於書無不窺，不靳靳守古法。

translations.literal: Yi's formulas did not trace to a single master; of books there was none he did not scrutinize; he did not rigidly cling to ancient methods.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's medical art did not follow any single master; he scrutinized every text he could find and refused to cling rigidly to ancient formulas.

sentences.zh: 時度越縱舍，卒與法會。

translations.literal: At times transgressing and deviating freely, in the end he accorded with the method.
translations.idiomatic: He often departed freely from convention, yet in the end his treatments matched the principles.

sentences.zh: 尤遽《本草》諸書，辨正闕誤。

translations.literal: He was especially quick with the Materia Medica and such books, correcting omissions and errors.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially versed in the Materia Medica and related works, correcting omissions and errors.

sentences.zh: 或得異藥，問之，必為言生出本末、物色、名貌差別之詳，退而考之皆合。

translations.literal: When someone obtained a rare drug and asked him, he invariably detailed its place of origin, appearance, name, and distinctions; upon later investigation all accorded.
translations.idiomatic: When asked about an unfamiliar drug, he invariably gave a detailed account of its origin, appearance, and distinguishing features—and later verification always confirmed his account.

sentences.zh: 末年攣痹浸劇，知不可為，召親戚訣別，易衣待盡，遂卒，年八十二。

translations.literal: In his final years cramps and numbness gradually grew severe; knowing nothing could be done, he summoned kin to farewell, changed clothes and awaited the end; he then died, aged eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In his final years his cramps and numbness worsened. Knowing the end was near, he summoned his kin to say farewell, changed into burial clothes, and waited peacefully. He died at eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 僧智緣，隨州人，善醫。

translations.literal: The monk Zhiyuan, a native of Suizhou, was skilled in medicine.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Zhiyuan, a native of Suizhou, was skilled in medicine.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐末，召至京師，舍於相國寺。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jiayou era he was summoned to the capital and lodged at Xiangguo Temple.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jiayou era he was summoned to the capital and lodged at Xiangguo Temple.

sentences.zh: 每察脈，知人貴賤、禍福、休咎，診父之脈而能道其子吉凶，所言若神，士大夫爭造之。

translations.literal: Whenever he examined pulses he knew people's noble and base status, fortune and misfortune, weal and woe; examining a father's pulse he could speak the son's good and ill fortune; his words were like the divine, and officials and gentry vied to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he took a patient's pulse he could discern rank, fortune, disaster, and blessing; from a father's pulse he could predict a son's fate. His pronouncements seemed supernatural, and officials flocked to consult him.

sentences.zh: 王珪與王安石在翰林，珪疑古無此，安石曰：“昔醫和診晉侯，而知其良臣將死。

translations.literal: Wang Gui and Wang Anshi were in the Hanlin Academy; Gui doubted antiquity had such a thing; Anshi said, "Formerly Physician He examined the ruler of Jin and knew his worthy minister would die.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui and Wang Anshi served in the Hanlin Academy. Gui doubted such things existed in antiquity, but Anshi said, "Physician He once examined the Duke of Jin and foretold the death of a worthy minister.

sentences.zh: 夫良臣之命乃見於其君之脈，則視父知子，亦何足怪哉！

translations.literal: Now the worthy minister's fate was seen in his lord's pulse—then seeing the father and knowing the son, what is there to marvel at!
translations.idiomatic: If a minister's fate could appear in his ruler's pulse, then reading a father to know a son is hardly surprising!

sentences.zh: 熙寧中，王韶謀取青唐，上言蕃族重僧，而僧結吳叱臘主部帳甚眾，請智緣與俱至邊。

translations.literal: During the Xining era, Wang Shao plotted to take Qingtang; he memorialized that the tribal peoples honored monks, and the monk Jiewuchila commanded many tribal encampments; he requested Zhiyuan go with him to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xining era Wang Shao sought to seize Qingtang. He memorialized that the tribes honored monks and that the monk Jiewuchila commanded many tribal encampments, requesting that Zhiyuan accompany him to the border.

sentences.zh: 神宗召見，賜白金，遣乘傳而西，遂稱“經略大師”。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong summoned and granted him, sent him by post horse westward, and he was styled "Great Master of Frontier Strategy."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong received him, granted him silver, and dispatched him west by imperial courier. He was styled "Great Master of Frontier Strategy."

sentences.zh: 智緣有辯口，徑入蕃中，說結吳叱臘歸化，而他族俞龍珂、禹藏訥令支等皆因以書款。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan had eloquence; he went straight into the tribes, persuaded Jiewuchila to submit, and other clans Yu Longke, Yuzang Ne Lingzhi and others all submitted pledges in writing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan was eloquent. He went directly among the tribes and persuaded Jiewuchila to submit; other chiefs including Yu Longke and Yuzang Ne Lingzhi followed with written pledges of allegiance.

sentences.zh: 韶頗忌惡之，言其撓邊事，召還，以為右街首坐，卒。

translations.literal: Shao greatly resented him, saying he obstructed frontier affairs; he was recalled and made head seat of the Right Street; he died.
translations.idiomatic: Shao deeply resented him, accusing him of obstructing frontier affairs. Zhiyuan was recalled and made chief priest of the Right Street monastery, where he died.

sentences.zh: 郭天信字佑之，開封人。

translations.literal: Guo Tianxin, courtesy name Youzhi, was a native of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tianxin, courtesy name Youzhi, was a native of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 以技隸太史局。

translations.literal: By his skill he was attached to the Directorate of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: By virtue of his skills he was attached to the Directorate of Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 徽宗為端王，嚐退朝，天信密遮白曰：“王當有天下。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huizong was Prince Duan, once after retiring from court Tianxin secretly intercepted him and said, "Your Highness is destined to rule the realm.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong was still Prince Duan, Tianxin once intercepted him privately after court and whispered, "Your Highness is destined to rule all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: ”既而即帝位，因得親昵。

translations.literal: " Shortly afterward he ascended the throne, and thereby became close and favored.
translations.idiomatic: " When Huizong took the throne, Tianxin became a close favorite.

sentences.zh: 不數年，至樞密都承旨、節度觀察留後。

translations.literal: Within a few years he reached Commissioner-in-Chief of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Military Commissioner and Observation Commissioner with acting status.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years he rose to Commissioner-in-Chief of the Bureau of Military Affairs and acting military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 其子中復為閣門通事舍人，許陪進士徑試大廷，擢秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: His son Zhongfu became Court Protocol Attendant; he was permitted to accompany jinshi candidates in direct palace examination and was promoted to Proofreader in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhongfu became a Court Protocol Attendant, was permitted to sit the palace examination alongside jinshi candidates, and was promoted to Secretariat proofreader.

sentences.zh: 未幾，天信覺已甚，乞還武爵，又從之。

translations.literal: Before long Tianxin felt he had gone too far and petitioned to relinquish his military rank; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Tianxin realized he had overreached and petitioned to surrender his military title; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 政和初，拜定武軍節度使、祐神觀使，頗與聞外朝政事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhenghe era he was appointed Military Commissioner of Dingwu Army and Commissioner of the Youshen Observatory, and was much involved in outer-court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenghe era he was appointed military commissioner of Dingwu and commissioner of the Youshen Observatory, and gained considerable influence over outer-court affairs.

sentences.zh: 見蔡京亂國，每托天文以撼之，且云：“日中有黑子。

translations.literal: Seeing Cai Jing ruining the state, he repeatedly invoked astronomy to shake him, saying moreover, "There is a black spot in the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Cai Jing's misrule, he repeatedly invoked celestial omens against him, declaring, "There is a black spot on the sun.

sentences.zh: ”帝甚懼，言之不已，京由是黜。

translations.literal: " The emperor was greatly afraid; he spoke of it incessantly; Jing was thereby dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was terrified; Tianxin repeated the claim until Cai Jing was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 張商英方有時望，天信往往稱於內朝。

translations.literal: Zhang Shangying then had timely renown; Tianxin often praised him in the inner court.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shangying then enjoyed rising prestige, and Tianxin often praised him within the inner court.

sentences.zh: 商英亦欲借左右遊談之助，陰與相結，使僧德洪輩道達語言。

translations.literal: Shangying also wished to borrow the help of attendants' casual talk; secretly they joined in alliance, sending monks like Dehong to convey messages.
translations.idiomatic: Shangying likewise sought allies among court attendants and secretly allied with Tianxin, using monks such as Dehong to relay messages.

sentences.zh: 商英勸帝節儉，稍裁抑僧寺，帝始敬畏之，而近侍積不樂，間言浸潤，眷日衰。

translations.literal: Shangying counseled the emperor on frugality and slightly curtailed monasteries; the emperor began to revere him, but attendants long displeased, slander gradually seeping in, favor daily declining.
translations.idiomatic: Shangying urged thrift and modest curbs on monasteries; the emperor initially respected him, but disgruntled attendants spread slander until imperial favor faded.

sentences.zh: 京黨因是告商英與天信漏泄禁中語言，天信先發端，窺伺上旨，動息必報，乃從外庭決之，無不如誌。

translations.literal: Jing's faction therefore reported that Shangying and Tianxin leaked forbidden inner-court speech; Tianxin first initiated it, spying on the emperor's intent, every movement reported; then from the outer court they decided matters, none failing to match intent.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's faction accused Shangying and Tianxin of leaking palace secrets—Tianxin eavesdropped on the emperor's intentions and relayed every move to Shangying, who then acted from the outer court with uncanny precision.

sentences.zh: 商英遂罷。

translations.literal: Shangying was then dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Shangying was promptly dismissed.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞張克公復論之，詔貶天信昭化軍節度副使、單州安置，命宋康年守單，幾其起居。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Zhang Kegong again memorialized; an edict demoted Tianxin to Vice Military Commissioner of Zhaohua Army and settled him at Danzhou; Song Kangnian was ordered to guard Dan and watch his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Zhang Kegong memorialized again; Tianxin was demoted to vice military commissioner of Zhaohua and exiled to Danzhou, with Song Kangnian assigned to monitor his conduct.

sentences.zh: 再貶行軍司馬，竄新州，又徒康年使廣東，天信至數月，死。

translations.literal: Again demoted to itinerant army marshal, banished to Xinzhou; Kangnian was also transferred to Guangdong; Tianxin arrived and within months died.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted again to army marshal and banished to Xinzhou; Kangnian was reassigned to Guangdong; Tianxin died within months of arrival.

sentences.zh: 京已再相，猶疑天信挾術多能，死未必實，令康年選吏發棺驗視焉。

translations.literal: Jing had again become chief minister; he still suspected Tianxin wielded arts with many powers, death not necessarily real; he ordered Kangnian to select officials to open the coffin and inspect.
translations.idiomatic: Jing, again chief minister, doubted Tianxin had faked his death through occult arts and ordered Kangnian to open the coffin for inspection.

sentences.zh: 魏漢津，本蜀黥卒也。

translations.literal: Wei Hanjin was originally a tattooed convict of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Hanjin was originally a tattooed convict from Shu.

sentences.zh: 自言師事唐仙人李良號“李八百”者，授以鼎樂之法。

translations.literal: He claimed to have studied under the Tang immortal Li Liang, styled "Li the Eight Hundred," who taught him the method of cauldron music.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed to have studied under the Tang immortal Li Liang, known as "Li the Eight Hundred," who taught him the art of cauldron alchemy and music.

sentences.zh: 嚐過三山龍門，聞水聲，謂人曰：“其下必有玉。

translations.literal: Once passing Longmen of Sanshan, hearing the sound of water, he told people, "Below there must be jade.
translations.idiomatic: Once near Longmen at Sanshan he heard rushing water and told others, "There must be jade beneath those waters.

sentences.zh: ”即脫衣沒水，抱石而出，果玉也。

translations.literal: " Immediately he stripped, entered the water, embraced a stone and came out—it was indeed jade.
translations.idiomatic: " He stripped, dove in, and emerged clutching a stone—it was indeed jade.

sentences.zh: 皇祐中，與房庶俱以善樂薦，時阮逸方定黍律，不獲用。

translations.literal: In the Huangyou era he and Fang Shu were both recommended for skill in music; at the time Ruan Yi was just setting the millet pitch-pipes and they were not employed.
translations.idiomatic: During Huangyou he and Fang Shu were recommended for musical talent, but Ruan Yi was then reforming pitch standards and they were not employed.

sentences.zh: 崇寧初猶在，朝廷方協考鍾律，得召見，獻樂議，言得黃帝，夏禹聲為律、身為度之說。
