translations.literal: Early in Chongning he was still alive; the court was jointly examining bell pitches; he was summoned, presented music proposals, speaking of obtaining the Yellow Emperor and Yu the Great's doctrine that sound defines pitch and the body defines measure.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chongning he was still active. The court was reviewing bell pitch standards; summoned to audience, he presented a music memorial reviving the doctrine that sound defines pitch and the body defines measure, attributed to the Yellow Emperor and Yu the Great.

sentences.zh: 謂人主稟賦與眾異，請以帝指三節三寸為度，定黃鍾之律；

translations.literal: He said the sovereign's endowment differs from the multitude; he requested taking the emperor's finger three joints and three inches as measure to fix the yellow bell pitch;
translations.idiomatic: He argued that the emperor's physical endowment differed from ordinary men and proposed measuring three joints and three inches of the imperial finger to fix the yellow bell pitch;

sentences.zh: 而中指之徑圍，則度量權衡所自出也。

translations.literal: And the middle finger's diameter and circumference—thence measures, weights, and balances originate.
translations.idiomatic: The diameter and circumference of the middle finger, he claimed, were the origin of all weights and measures.

sentences.zh: 又云：“聲有太有少。

translations.literal: He also said, "Sound has greater and lesser.
translations.idiomatic: He further said, "Sound divides into greater and lesser tones.

sentences.zh: 太者，清聲，陽也。

translations.literal: The greater is clear sound, yang.
translations.idiomatic: The greater is the clear tone—yang.

sentences.zh: 天道也。

translations.literal: It is the Way of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: This represents the Way of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 少者，濁聲，陰也，地道也。

translations.literal: The lesser is muddy sound, yin—it is the Way of Earth.
translations.idiomatic: The lesser is the muddy tone—yin, the Way of Earth.

sentences.zh: 中聲在其間，人道也。

translations.literal: The middle sound lies between them—it is the Way of Man.
translations.idiomatic: The middle tone between them represents the Way of Man.

sentences.zh: 合三才之道，備陰陽奇偶，然後四序可得而調，萬物可得而理。

translations.literal: Combining the Way of the three powers, complete with yin-yang and odd-even, then the four seasons can be regulated and the myriad things can be ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Uniting the three cosmic forces and balancing yin-yang and odd-even pairings, the four seasons could be harmonized and all things brought into order.

sentences.zh: ”當時以為迂怪，蔡京獨神之。

translations.literal: " At the time it was deemed abstruse and strange; Cai Jing alone regarded it as divine.
translations.idiomatic: " Contemporaries found this far-fetched, but Cai Jing alone treated it as revelation.

sentences.zh: 或言漢津本範鎮之役，稍窺見其製作，而京托之於李良雲。

translations.literal: Some said Hanjin was originally in Fan Zhen's service, slightly glimpsing his productions, while Jing ascribed them to Li Liang, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Some claimed Hanjin had been Fan Zhen's servant and borrowed his methods, while Jing credited Li Liang instead.

sentences.zh: 於是請先鑄九鼎，次鑄帝坐大鍾及二十四氣鍾。

translations.literal: Thereupon he requested first casting the Nine Cauldrons, next casting the Emperor's Seat great bell and the twenty-four seasonal qi bells.
translations.idiomatic: He then proposed casting the Nine Cauldrons first, followed by the great bell of the Imperial Seat and twenty-four seasonal bells.

sentences.zh: 四年三月鼎成，賜號衝顯處士。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year the cauldrons were completed; he was granted the title Revealing Worthy Recluse.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fourth year the cauldrons were completed and he received the title Revealing Worthy Recluse.

sentences.zh: 八月，《大晟樂》成。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the Dasheng Music was completed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Dasheng Music was completed.

sentences.zh: 徽宗禦大慶殿受群臣朝賀，加漢津虛和衝顯寶應先生，頒其樂書天下。

translations.literal: Emperor Huizong presided at Daqing Hall receiving officials' congratulations; Hanjin was advanced to Master of Empty Harmony, Revealing Treasure Response; his music book was promulgated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huizong received felicitations at Daqing Hall, elevated Hanjin to Master of Empty Harmony and Revealing Treasure Response, and promulgated his music treatise empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 而京之客劉昺主樂事，論太少之說為非，將議改作。

translations.literal: But Jing's client Liu Bing headed music affairs and argued the greater-lesser doctrine was wrong, about to discuss revision.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's protégé Liu Bing oversaw music affairs and disputed the greater-lesser doctrine, proposing revisions.

sentences.zh: 既而以樂成久，易之恐動觀聽，遂止。

translations.literal: Yet because the music had long been completed, changing it feared disturbing observers and listeners; they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: But the music had stood so long that revision risked unsettling public opinion, and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 漢津密為京言：“《大晟》獨得古意什三四爾，他多非古說，異日當以訪任宗堯。

translations.literal: Hanjin secretly told Jing, "The Dasheng alone obtains ancient intent three or four parts in ten; the rest mostly departs from ancient doctrine; another day you should consult Ren Zongyao.
translations.idiomatic: Hanjin privately told Jing, "The Dasheng system captures perhaps thirty or forty percent of ancient intent; much of the rest deviates from antiquity—you should consult Ren Zongyao someday.

sentences.zh: ”宗堯學於漢津者也。

translations.literal: " Zongyao was one who studied under Hanjin.
translations.idiomatic: " Ren Zongyao had been Hanjin's pupil.

sentences.zh: 漢津曉陰陽數術，多奇中，嚐語所知曰：“不三十年，天下亂矣。

translations.literal: Hanjin understood yin-yang and numerical arts, many strange hits; once he told acquaintances, "Within thirty years the realm will be in chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Hanjin mastered yin-yang numerology and often proved astonishingly accurate. He once told acquaintances, "Within thirty years the empire will fall into chaos.

sentences.zh: ”未幾死。

translations.literal: " Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: " He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 京遂召宗堯為典樂，復欲有所建，而為田為所奪，語在《樂志》。

translations.literal: Jing then summoned Zongyao as music director, again wishing to build something, but Tian Wei seized it—the account is in the Music Treatise.
translations.idiomatic: Jing then appointed Zongyao director of music and sought further innovations, but Tian Wei blocked him—the account appears in the Music Treatise.

sentences.zh: 後即鑄鼎之所建寶成殿，祀黃帝、夏禹、成王、周、召而良、漢津俱配食。

translations.literal: Later at the place where the cauldrons were cast they built Baocheng Hall, sacrificing to the Yellow Emperor, Yu the Great, King Cheng, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao, while Liang and Hanjin both received accompanying offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at the site where the cauldrons were cast, they built Baocheng Hall to honor the Yellow Emperor, Yu the Great, King Cheng, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao, with Liang and Hanjin receiving accompanying sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 諡漢津為嘉晟侯。

translations.literal: Hanjin was posthumously titled Marquis Jiasheng.
translations.idiomatic: Hanjin was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis Jiasheng.

sentences.zh: 有馬賁者，出京之門，在大晟府十三年，方魏、劉、任、田異論時，依違其間，無所質正，擢至通議大夫、徽猷閣待制。

translations.literal: There was Ma Ben, who came from Jing's school; in the Dasheng Office thirteen years, when Wei, Liu, Ren, and Tian disputed with differing views, he wavered between them, correcting nothing, yet was promoted to Supervisory Censor and Attendant Drafting at the Huiyao Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Ben, a protégé of Cai Jing, served thirteen years in the Dasheng Office. When Wei, Liu, Ren, and Tian disputed music theory, he vacillated among them without taking a stand, yet rose to Supervisory Censor and Attendant Drafting at the Huiyao Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 議者咎當時名器之濫如此。

translations.literal: Critics blamed the abuse of honors and offices at the time as being like this.
translations.idiomatic: Critics blamed such cases for the era's debasement of honors and offices.

sentences.zh: 王老誌，濮州臨泉人。

translations.literal: Wang Laozhi, a native of Linquan in Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Laozhi was a native of Linquan in Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 事親以孝聞。

translations.literal: He was known for filial service to his parents.
translations.idiomatic: He was renowned for filial devotion to his parents.

sentences.zh: 為轉運小吏，不受賂謝。

translations.literal: As a minor clerk in transport he accepted no bribes or gifts of thanks.
translations.idiomatic: As a minor transport clerk he accepted no bribes or gifts.

sentences.zh: 遇異人於丐中，自言：“吾所謂鍾離先生也。

translations.literal: He met an extraordinary man among beggars, who said of himself, "I am the one called Master Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: Among beggars he met an extraordinary man who declared, "I am the one called Master Zhongli.

sentences.zh: ”予之丹，服之而狂。

translations.literal: " He gave him a pill; after taking it he went mad.
translations.idiomatic: " The stranger gave him an elixir; after swallowing it he grew frenzied.

sentences.zh: 遂棄妻子，結草廬田間，時為人言休咎。

translations.literal: Thereupon he abandoned wife and children, built a thatched hut in the fields, and from time to time told people fortune and misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: He abandoned his wife and children, built a thatched hut in the fields, and began foretelling fortune and disaster.

sentences.zh: 政和三年，太仆卿王亶以其名聞。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenghe, Grand Master of Steeds Wang Dan reported his name.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenghe, Grand Master of Steeds Wang Dan reported his name to court.

sentences.zh: 召至京師，館於蔡京第。

translations.literal: He was summoned to the capital and lodged at Cai Jing's mansion.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the capital and housed in Cai Jing's mansion.

sentences.zh: 嚐緘書一封至帝所，徽宗啟讀，乃昔歲秋中與喬、劉二妃燕好之語也。

translations.literal: Once he sealed a letter delivered to the emperor; Huizong opened and read it—it was language of intimate pleasure with the Qiao and Liu consorts from the previous autumn.
translations.idiomatic: He once delivered a sealed letter to the emperor; when Huizong opened it, he found intimate words exchanged with Consorts Qiao and Liu the previous autumn.

sentences.zh: 帝由是稍信之，封為洞微先生。

translations.literal: The emperor thereby slightly believed him and enfeoffed him as Master of Cave Profundity.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was partly convinced and enfeoffed him as Master of Cave Profundity.

sentences.zh: 朝士多從求書，初若不可解，後卒應者十八九，故其門如市。

translations.literal: Officials mostly sought letters from him; at first they seemed incomprehensible, but later eight or nine in ten proved true; therefore his gate was like a market.
translations.idiomatic: Officials flocked to him for written oracles; though cryptic at first, eight or nine in ten later proved true, and his door became thronged like a marketplace.

sentences.zh: 京慮太甚，頗以為戒；

translations.literal: Jing feared it had gone too far and took it somewhat as a warning;
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing feared matters had gone too far and grew wary;

sentences.zh: 老誌亦謹畏，乃奏禁絕之。

translations.literal: Laozhi also was cautious and fearful; he then memorialized to forbid and abolish it.
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi himself grew cautious and petitioned to ban the practice.

sentences.zh: 嚐獻乾坤鑒法，命鑄之。

translations.literal: Once he presented the method of the Qiankun Mirror; he was ordered to cast it.
translations.idiomatic: He once presented the method of the Cosmic Mirror and was ordered to have it cast.

sentences.zh: 既成，謂帝與皇后他日皆有難，請時坐鑒下，思所以儆懼消變者。

translations.literal: When it was finished, he said the emperor and empress would both face calamity on another day, and asked that they sit beneath the mirror from time to time and consider means of warning, fear, and dispelling the transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Once it was cast, he warned that the emperor and empress would both meet calamity in days to come, and urged them to sit beneath the mirror from time to time and reflect on what might inspire vigilance and avert disaster.

sentences.zh: 明年，見其師，責以擅處富貴，乃丐歸，未得請，病甚，始許其去。

translations.literal: The next year he saw his master, who rebuked him for presuming to dwell amid wealth and rank; he then begged to return home but was not granted permission; when his illness grew severe, permission to leave was finally granted.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he saw his master, who upbraided him for seeking wealth and status unbecomingly. He begged to go home but was refused; only when his illness grew severe was he at last allowed to leave.

sentences.zh: 步行出，就居，病已失矣。

translations.literal: He walked out on foot, took up residence, and his illness was already gone.
translations.idiomatic: He walked out on foot, settled into his dwelling, and his illness was already gone.

sentences.zh: 歸濮而死。

translations.literal: He returned to Pu and died.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to Pu and died there.

sentences.zh: 詔賜金以葬，贈正議大夫。

translations.literal: An edict granted gold for his burial and posthumously conferred Right Policy Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: By edict he was granted gold for burial and posthumously made Right Policy Grandee.

sentences.zh: 初，王黼未達時，父為臨泉令，問黼名位所至，即書“太平宰相”四字。

translations.literal: At first, when Wang Fu had not yet risen, his father was magistrate of Linquan; asked how far Fu's name and rank would reach, he immediately wrote the four characters "Peaceful-Era Grand Counselor."
translations.idiomatic: Early on, before Wang Fu had risen to power, his father served as magistrate of Linquan. When asked how far his son's name and rank would go, he at once wrote the four characters "Grand Counselor of a Peaceful Age."

sentences.zh: 旋以墨塗去之，曰：“恐泄機也。

translations.literal: Immediately he covered it over with ink and said, "I fear the secret would leak out."
translations.idiomatic: He immediately smeared the words over with ink and said, "I fear it would reveal the secret."

sentences.zh: ”黼敗，人乃悟。

translations.literal: When Fu fell, people then understood.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu fell from power, people understood at last.

sentences.zh: 王仔昔，洪州人。

translations.literal: Wang Zixi was a man of Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zixi was from Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 始學儒，自言遇許遜，得《大洞》、《隱書》豁落七元之法，出遊嵩山，能道人未來事。

translations.literal: At first he studied Confucian learning; he said of himself that he met Xu Xun and obtained the methods of the Great Cavern and Hidden Scripture for the Seven Primordials of Huoluo; he went out to wander Mount Song and could tell people things of the future.
translations.idiomatic: He first studied Confucian learning, then claimed to have met Xu Xun and received the esoteric methods of the Great Cavern and Hidden Scripture concerning the Seven Primordials. Traveling Mount Song, he could foretell what lay ahead.

sentences.zh: 政和中，徽宗召見，賜號衝隱處士。

translations.literal: In the Zhenghe era, Huizong summoned and received him and granted the title Recluse of Penetrating Hiddenness.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenghe era Huizong summoned him to audience and gave him the title Recluse of Penetrating Hiddenness.

sentences.zh: 帝以旱禱雨，每遣小黃門持紙求仔昔畫，日又至，忽篆符其上，仍細書“焚符湯沃而洗之”。

translations.literal: Because of drought the emperor prayed for rain and each day sent minor yellow-gate attendants bearing paper to request a drawing from Zixi; when the day came again, a talisman was suddenly seal-scripted upon it, with a fine inscription reading "Burn the talisman, boil water, rinse, and wash with it."
translations.idiomatic: During a drought the emperor prayed for rain, sending minor palace attendants each day with paper for Zixi to inscribe. When the day came again, a talisman appeared on it in seal script, along with a fine note: "Burn the talisman, boil the water, rinse, and wash with it."

sentences.zh: 黃門懼不肯受，強之，乃持去。

translations.literal: The yellow-gate attendant feared and would not accept it; he was forced, and then carried it away.
translations.idiomatic: The attendant was afraid and refused to take it, but was pressed until he did.

sentences.zh: 蓋帝默祝為宮妃療赤目者，用其說一沃，立愈。

translations.literal: In fact the emperor had silently prayed to treat a palace consort's red eyes; following his instructions with one rinsing, she was immediately cured.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had secretly prayed for a cure for a palace consort's inflamed eyes; a single washing as directed effected an immediate cure.

sentences.zh: 進封通妙先生，居上清寶籙宮。

translations.literal: He was advanced to the title Master of Penetrating Wonder and dwelt at the Supreme Clarity Precious Register Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was further enfeoffed as Master of Penetrating Wonder and took up residence in the Supreme Clarity Precious Register Palace.

sentences.zh: 獻議九鼎神器不可藏於外。

translations.literal: He presented a proposal that the Nine Cauldrons, vessels of divine regalia, must not be stored outside.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that the Nine Cauldrons—the sacred regalia—must not be kept outside the palace.

sentences.zh: 乃於禁中建圓象徽調閣以貯之。

translations.literal: Thereupon within the Forbidden precincts they built the Round Image Emblem Harmony Pavilion to store them.
translations.idiomatic: A Round Image Emblem Harmony Pavilion was then built within the Forbidden City to house them.

sentences.zh: 仔昔資倨傲，又少戇，帝常待以客禮，故其遇巨閹殆若童奴，又欲群道士皆宗己。

translations.literal: Zixi's nature was haughty and proud, and he was also somewhat simple; the emperor often treated him with guest rites, so in meeting great eunuchs he was nearly like a child or slave; he also wished all Daoist priests to take him as their master.
translations.idiomatic: Zixi was arrogant by nature and somewhat simple-minded. Because the emperor often treated him as an honored guest, he dealt with senior eunuchs almost like a child ordering servants, and sought to make all Daoist priests defer to him.

sentences.zh: 及林靈素有寵，忌之，陷以事，囚之東太一宮。

translations.literal: When Lin Lingsu came into favor, he envied him, framed him on a charge, and imprisoned him in the Eastern Grand Unity Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin Lingsu rose to favor, he envied Zixi, framed him on a charge, and had him imprisoned in the Eastern Grand Unity Palace.

sentences.zh: 旋坐言語不遜，下獄死。

translations.literal: Shortly he was convicted for irreverent speech, sent down to prison, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon convicted of disrespectful speech, thrown into prison, and died there.

sentences.zh: 仔昔之得罪，宦者馮浩力最多。

translations.literal: In Zixi's falling into guilt, the eunuch Feng Hao's effort was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: Of those responsible for Zixi's downfall, the eunuch Feng Hao did the most.

sentences.zh: 未死時，書示其徒曰：“上蔡遇冤人。

translations.literal: Before he died, he wrote and showed his disciples, saying, "At Shangcai one meets a man wronged."
translations.idiomatic: Before his death he wrote to his disciples: "At Shangcai you will meet a man who has been wronged."

sentences.zh: ”其後浩南竄，至上蔡被誅。

translations.literal: Later Hao was exiled south; when he reached Shangcai he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Later Feng Hao was banished south; at Shangcai he was put to death.

sentences.zh: 林靈素，溫州人。

translations.literal: Lin Lingsu was a man of Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Lingsu was from Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 少從浮屠學，苦其師笞罵，去為道士。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under Buddhist monks; suffering his master's beatings and scoldings, he left and became a Daoist priest.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied with Buddhist monks, but weary of his master's beatings and abuse he left and became a Daoist priest.

sentences.zh: 善妖幻，往來淮、泗間，丐食僧寺，僧寺苦之。

translations.literal: He was skilled at demonic illusions; traveling between the Huai and Si rivers, he begged food at Buddhist monasteries, and the monasteries found him a nuisance.
translations.idiomatic: He practiced sorcery and illusion, wandering between the Huai and Si rivers to beg food at monasteries, which soon wearied of him.

sentences.zh: 政和末，王老誌、王仔昔既衰，徽宗訪方士於左道錄徐知常，以靈素對。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenghe, as Wang Laozhi and Wang Zixi had declined, Huizong inquired of Daoist masters from Left Dao Registrar Xu Zhichang, who named Lingsu in reply.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Zhenghe era, as Wang Laozhi and Wang Zixi waned in influence, Huizong asked Left Dao Registrar Xu Zhichang for a master of the arts; Xu recommended Lingsu.

sentences.zh: 既見，大言曰：“天有九霄，而神霄為最高，其治曰府。

translations.literal: Once received in audience, he spoke grandly, saying, "Heaven has nine empyrean realms, and the Divine Empyrean is highest; its administration is called the Office."
translations.idiomatic: At audience he spoke grandly: "Heaven has nine empyrean realms, of which the Divine Empyrean is highest; its seat of government is called the Office."

sentences.zh: 神霄玉清王者，上帝之長子，主南方，號長生大帝君，陛下是也，既下降於世，其弟號青華帝君者，主東方，攝領之。

translations.literal: The Jade Pure King of the Divine Empyrean is the Supreme Sovereign's eldest son, governing the south, titled Great Sovereign Lord of Long Life—the Majesty is he; having already descended into the world, his younger brother titled Sovereign Lord of Azure Splendor governs the east and assists in ruling.
translations.idiomatic: The Jade Pure King of the Divine Empyrean is the Supreme Sovereign's eldest son, ruler of the south, known as the Great Sovereign Lord of Long Life—that is Your Majesty, descended into this world. His younger brother, the Sovereign Lord of Azure Splendor, rules the east and shares in the governance.

sentences.zh: 己乃府仙卿曰褚慧，亦下降佐帝君之治。

translations.literal: I am the Office Immortal Minister called Chu Hui, who also descended to assist the Sovereign Lord's governance.
translations.idiomatic: As for myself, I am the Office Immortal Minister named Chu Hui, likewise descended to assist the Sovereign Lord in governing.

sentences.zh: ”又謂蔡京為左元仙伯，王黼為文華吏，盛章、王革為園苑寶華吏，鄭居中、童貫及諸巨閹皆為之名。

translations.literal: He also declared Cai Jing Left Origin Immortal Lord, Wang Fu Literary Splendor Clerk, Sheng Zhang and Wang Ge Garden Precious Splendor Clerks, and gave names to Zheng Juzhong, Tong Guan, and all the great eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: He also named Cai Jing Left Origin Immortal Lord, Wang Fu Literary Splendor Clerk, Sheng Zhang and Wang Ge Garden Precious Splendor Clerks, and assigned celestial titles to Zheng Juzhong, Tong Guan, and the senior eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 貴妃劉氏方有寵，曰九華玉真安妃。

translations.literal: The honored consort Lady Liu, then in favor, he called Nine Splendor Jade True Peace Consort.
translations.idiomatic: The favored consort Lady Liu he styled the Nine Splendor Jade True Peace Consort.

sentences.zh: 帝心獨喜其事，賜號通真達靈先生，賞賚無算。

translations.literal: The emperor alone delighted in this affair at heart, granted the title Master of Penetrating Truth and Attaining Spirit, and rewarded him beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor alone took delight in these claims, enfeoffed him as Master of Penetrating Truth and Attaining Spirit, and showered him with rewards beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 建上清寶籙宮，密連禁省。

translations.literal: They built the Supreme Clarity Precious Register Palace, secretly connected to the Forbidden inner quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The Supreme Clarity Precious Register Palace was built, linked in secret to the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 天下皆建神霄萬壽宮。

translations.literal: Throughout the realm Divine Empyrean Longevity Palaces were built.
translations.idiomatic: Divine Empyrean Longevity Palaces were erected across the empire.

sentences.zh: 浸浸造為青華正晝臨壇，及火龍神劍夜降內宮之事，假帝誥、天書、雲篆，務以欺世惑眾。

translations.literal: Gradually he fabricated matters such as the Azure Splendor rite at noon upon the altar and the descent by night of the Fire Dragon Divine Sword into the inner palace, using feigned imperial edicts, heavenly writs, and cloud seal-script to deceive the world and beguile the masses.
translations.idiomatic: Gradually he invented tales of the Azure Splendor altar rite at midday and of the Fire Dragon Divine Sword descending by night into the inner palace, wielding forged imperial edicts, heavenly scriptures, and cloud talismans to mislead the world.

sentences.zh: 其說妄誕，不可究質，實無所能解。

translations.literal: His doctrines were wild and absurd, impossible to investigate to their basis; in truth he could resolve nothing.
translations.idiomatic: His teachings were absurd beyond verification; in truth he could accomplish almost nothing.

sentences.zh: 惟稍識五雷法，召呼風霆，間禱雨有小驗而已。

translations.literal: Only he knew somewhat the Five Thunder rite, could summon wind and thunder, and when praying for rain occasionally had slight success, that was all.
translations.idiomatic: He knew something of the Five Thunder rite and could call up wind and thunder; when praying for rain he occasionally had modest success—and that was all.

sentences.zh: 令吏民詣宮受神霄秘錄，朝士之嗜進者，亦靡然趨之。

translations.literal: He ordered officials and commoners to come to the palace to receive the Divine Empyrean secret registers; court officials eager for advancement also flocked to it in droves.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered officials and commoners to attend the palace for Divine Empyrean secret registers, and ambitious courtiers joined the rush.

sentences.zh: 每設大齋，輒費緡錢數萬，謂之千道會。

translations.literal: Whenever he held a great fast he spent tens of thousands in strings of cash, calling it the Thousand-Dao Assembly.
translations.idiomatic: Each great fasting ceremony cost tens of thousands of strings of cash and was called the Thousand-Dao Assembly.

sentences.zh: 帝設幄其側，而靈素升高正坐，問者皆再拜以請。

translations.literal: The emperor set up a canopy at his side while Lingsu ascended high and sat facing front; questioners all bowed twice to ask.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sat under a canopy at his side while Lingsu mounted the dais and took the high seat; all who asked questions bowed twice before speaking.

sentences.zh: 所言無殊異，時時雜捷給嘲詼以資媟笑。

translations.literal: What he said was nothing extraordinary; from time to time he mixed in quick wit and mockery to supply impious laughter.
translations.idiomatic: His answers were unremarkable, though he often spiced them with quick wit and banter to provoke ribald laughter.

sentences.zh: 其徒美衣玉食，幾二萬人。

translations.literal: His followers dressed in fine clothes and ate jade-like feasts—nearly twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: His followers numbered nearly twenty thousand, living in fine dress and lavish fare.

sentences.zh: 遂立道學，置郎、大夫十等，有諸殿侍晨、校籍、授經，以擬待制、修撰、直閣。

translations.literal: Thereupon Daoist learning was established; they set ten ranks of Gentleman and Grandee, with positions such as palace attendant-of-the-dawn, registrar, and scripture instructor, modeled on awaiting-draftsman, compiler, and direct access to the library pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: A Daoist school was established with ten ranks of Gentleman and Grandee, including Palace Attendant-of-the-Dawn, registrar, and scripture instructor, patterned on the awaiting-draftsman, compiler, and direct access posts of the civil service.

sentences.zh: 始欲盡廢釋氏以逞前憾，既而改其名稱冠服。

translations.literal: At first he wished to abolish Buddhism entirely to vent an old grievance; afterward he only changed its names, caps, and robes.
translations.idiomatic: At first he wanted to abolish Buddhism outright to settle an old grudge, but in the end he settled for renaming its institutions and altering its dress.

sentences.zh: 靈素益尊重，升溫州為應道軍節度，加號元妙先生、金門羽客、衝和殿侍晨，出入嗬引，至與諸王爭道。

translations.literal: Lingsu grew ever more honored; Wenzhou was elevated to Yingdao military commission; additional titles were added—Master of Original Wonder, Feathered Guest of the Golden Gate, Attendant-of-the-Dawn of the Harmonious Assault Hall; when going out callers cleared the way, until he even contended for the road with the princes.
translations.idiomatic: Lingsu grew ever more exalted. Wenzhou was raised to the Yingdao military command; he received further titles—Master of Original Wonder, Feathered Guest of the Golden Gate, Attendant-of-the-Dawn of the Harmonious Assault Hall. Criers cleared his path wherever he went, and he even vied with princes for right of way.

sentences.zh: 都人稱曰：“道家兩府。

translations.literal: The people of the capital called them, "The Two Offices of the Daoist sect."
translations.idiomatic: The people of the capital called them "the two seats of Daoist power."

sentences.zh: ”本與道士王允誠共為怪神，後忌其相軋，毒之死。

translations.literal: He had originally joined the Daoist priest Wang Yuncheng in trafficking with strange spirits; later, envying their mutual rivalry, he poisoned him to death.
translations.idiomatic: He had once partnered with the Daoist Wang Yuncheng in conjuring strange spirits, but later, fearing a rival, poisoned him to death.

sentences.zh: 宣和初，都城暴水，遣靈素厭勝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xuanhe, when the capital was struck by flooding, Lingsu was dispatched to perform suppression by occult means.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xuanhe era, when the capital was flooded, Lingsu was sent to quell the disaster by occult rites.

sentences.zh: 方率其徒步虛城上，役夫爭舉梃將擊之，走而免。

translations.literal: Just as he was striding atop the floodwall in his bare feet, laborers struggled to raise clubs and were about to strike him; he fled and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: As he strutted barefoot atop the floodwall, laborers raised clubs to beat him; he fled and escaped.

sentences.zh: 帝知眾所怨，始不樂。

translations.literal: The emperor knew the people resented him and for the first time was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Learning how widely he was resented, the emperor turned against him for the first time.

sentences.zh: 靈素在京師四年，恣橫愈不悛，道遇皇太子弗斂避。

translations.literal: Lingsu had been in the capital four years, growing ever more unrestrained without repentance; encountering the crown prince on the road he did not defer and withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: After four years in the capital Lingsu grew ever more overbearing; meeting the crown prince on the road he refused to step aside.

sentences.zh: 太子入訴，帝怒，以為太虛大夫，斥還故裏，命江端本通判溫州，幾察之。

translations.literal: The crown prince entered and complained; the emperor was angered, made him Grand Void Grandee, banished him to his former home, and ordered Jiang Duanben as vice-prefect of Wenzhou secretly to investigate him.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince complained to the emperor, who in anger demoted him to Grand Void Grandee, sent him back to his hometown, and ordered Jiang Duanben, vice-prefect of Wenzhou, to investigate him covertly.

sentences.zh: 端本廉得其居處過製罪，詔徙置楚州而已死。

translations.literal: Duanben through investigation learned the crime of excessive scale in his dwelling; an edict ordered relocation to Chuzhou, but he was already dead.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Duanben uncovered crimes arising from the excessive grandeur of his residence; an edict ordered his transfer to Chuzhou, but by then he was already dead.

sentences.zh: 遺奏至，猶以侍從禮葬焉。

translations.literal: When his final memorial arrived, he was still buried with the rites due an attendant-of-the-court.
translations.idiomatic: When his final memorial arrived, he was nonetheless buried with the honors due a court attendant.

sentences.zh: 皇甫坦，蜀之夾江人。

translations.literal: Huang Futan was a man of Jiajiang in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Futan was from Jiajiang in Shu.

sentences.zh: 善醫術。

translations.literal: He was skilled in the medical art.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in medicine.

sentences.zh: 顯仁太后苦目疾，國醫不能療，詔募他醫，臨安守臣張偁以坦聞。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Xianren suffered from eye disease; the imperial physicians could not treat it; an edict recruited other physicians, and Lin'an prefect Zhang Cheng reported Tan's name.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Xianren suffered from an eye ailment that court physicians could not cure. An edict sought doctors from outside the palace, and the Lin'an prefect Zhang Cheng recommended Huang Futan.

sentences.zh: 高宗召見，問何以治身，坦曰：“心無為則身安，人主無為則天下治。

translations.literal: Gaozong summoned and received him, asking how to treat the body; Tan said, "When the heart is without deliberate action the body is at peace; when the ruler is without deliberate action the realm is governed."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong summoned him and asked how one should care for the body. Tan answered, "When the heart is without deliberate action, the body is at peace; when the ruler acts without interference, the realm is well governed."

sentences.zh: ”引至慈寧殿治太后目疾，立愈。

translations.literal: He was led to Cining Hall to treat the empress dowager's eye disease, and she was immediately cured.
translations.idiomatic: He was taken to Cining Hall to treat the empress dowager's eyes and cured her at once.

sentences.zh: 帝喜，厚賜之，一無所受。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and richly rewarded him, but he accepted none of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and offered rich rewards, but Huang Futan declined everything.

sentences.zh: 令持香禱青城山，還，復召問以長生久視之術，坦曰：“先禁諸欲，勿令放逸。

translations.literal: He was ordered to burn incense and pray at Mount Qingcheng; on return he was again summoned and asked about the art of long life and enduring vision; Tan said, "First restrain all desires and do not let them run loose."
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to offer incense and pray at Mount Qingcheng. On his return he was summoned again and questioned about the art of long life; Tan said, "First curb every desire and do not let the mind wander free."

sentences.zh: 丹經萬卷，不如守一。

translations.literal: Ten thousand volumes of elixir scripture are not as good as guarding the One.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand volumes of alchemical scripture are worth less than holding fast to the One.

sentences.zh: ”帝歎服，書“清靜”二字以名其庵，且繪其像禁中。

translations.literal: The emperor sighed in admiration, wrote the two characters "Pure Stillness" to name his hermitage, and also had his portrait painted within the Forbidden precincts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed in admiration, inscribed the characters "Pure Stillness" as the name of his hermitage, and had his portrait painted in the palace.

sentences.zh: 荊南帥李道雅敬坦，坦歲謁道。

translations.literal: Jingnan commander Li Daoya respected Tan; Tan each year visited Dao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Daoya, military commissioner of Jingnan, held Huang Futan in esteem, and Tan visited him each year.

sentences.zh: 隆興初，道入朝，高宗、孝宗問之，皆稱皇甫先生而不名。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longxing, when Dao entered court, Gaozong and Xiaozong inquired about him and both called him Master Huangfu without using his personal name.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Longxing era, when Li Daoya came to court, both Gaozong and Xiaozong asked after Huang Futan and referred to him respectfully as Master Huangfu, never by personal name.

sentences.zh: 坦又善相人，嚐相道中女必為天下母，後果為光宗後。

translations.literal: Tan was also skilled at physiognomy; he once physiognomized Dao's daughter as destined to become mother of the realm; afterward she indeed became Guangzong's empress.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Futan was also skilled at reading faces. He once told Li Daoya that his daughter was destined to become empress of the realm; she later became Empress of Emperor Guangzong.

sentences.zh: 王克明字彥昭，其始饒州樂平人，後徙湖州烏程縣。

translations.literal: Wang Keming, styled Yanzhao, was originally a man of Leping in Raozhou; afterward he moved to Wucheng County in Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Keming, style name Yanzhao, was originally from Leping in Raozhou and later moved to Wucheng County in Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 紹興、乾道間名醫也。

translations.literal: He was a famous physician between the Shaoxing and Qiandao eras.
translations.idiomatic: He was a renowned physician of the Shaoxing and Qiandao eras.

sentences.zh: 初生時，母乏乳，餌以粥，遂得脾胃疾，長益甚，醫以為不可治。

translations.literal: When newly born his mother lacked milk; he was fed on gruel and thereby contracted spleen-and-stomach disease; as he grew it worsened, and physicians deemed it incurable.
translations.idiomatic: At birth his mother had no milk, so he was fed gruel and developed a chronic spleen-and-stomach disorder that worsened as he grew; physicians declared it incurable.

sentences.zh: 克明自讀《難經》、《素問》以求其法，刻意處藥，其病乃愈。

translations.literal: Keming himself read the Classic of Difficult Issues and Plain Questions to seek the method, deliberately prepared medicines, and his illness was then cured.
translations.idiomatic: Keming studied the Classic of Difficult Issues and the Plain Questions on his own, carefully compounded his medicines, and cured himself.

sentences.zh: 始以術行江、淮，入蘇、湖，針灸尤精。

translations.literal: At first he practiced his art along the Yangzi and Huai, entering Suzhou and Lake regions; he was especially skilled in acupuncture and moxibustion.
translations.idiomatic: He first practiced along the Yangzi and Huai, then in Suzhou and the lake country, and was especially masterful at acupuncture and moxibustion.

sentences.zh: 診脈有難療者，必沉思得其要，然後予之藥。

translations.literal: When pulse diagnosis revealed cases hard to cure, he always pondered deeply until he grasped the crucial point, and only then gave medicine.
translations.idiomatic: When a pulse reading pointed to a difficult case, he would reflect until he had grasped the root of the illness, and only then prescribe.

sentences.zh: 病雖數證，或用一藥以除其本，本除而餘病自去。

translations.literal: Though an illness might show several symptoms, sometimes one medicine was used to remove the root; once the root was removed the remaining diseases departed of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Even when several symptoms were present, he might use a single medicine to strike at the root; once the root was gone, the rest resolved themselves.

sentences.zh: 亦有不予藥者，期以某日自安。

translations.literal: There were also cases where he gave no medicine but fixed a date on which recovery would come of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he prescribed no medicine at all, telling the patient that on a certain day the illness would pass on its own.

sentences.zh: 有以為非藥之過，過在某事，當隨其事治之。

translations.literal: Some he held were not faults of medicine—the fault lay in some matter—and treatment should follow that matter.
translations.idiomatic: Some ailments, he held, were not medical failures at all; the fault lay in some other cause, and that cause had to be addressed.

sentences.zh: 言無不驗。

translations.literal: His words never failed to prove true.
translations.idiomatic: None of his predictions ever failed.

sentences.zh: 士大夫皆自屈與遊。

translations.literal: Scholar-officials all humbled themselves to associate with him.
translations.idiomatic: Scholar-officials willingly sought his company.

sentences.zh: 魏安行妻風痿十年不起，克明施針，而步履如初。

translations.literal: Wei Anxing's wife had wind paralysis for ten years and could not rise; Keming applied needles, and she walked as at first.
translations.idiomatic: The wife of Wei Anxing had been paralyzed by wind affliction for ten years; Keming needled her, and she walked again as she once had.

sentences.zh: 胡秉妻病氣秘腹脹，號呼逾旬，克明視之。

translations.literal: Hu Bing's wife suffered qi stagnation with abdominal distension, cried out for more than ten days; Keming examined her.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Bing's wife suffered painful bloating from blocked qi and had been writhing in agony for more than ten days when Keming examined her.

sentences.zh: 時秉家方會食，克明謂秉曰：“吾愈恭人病，使預會可乎？

translations.literal: At the time Bing's household was just at a gathering meal; Keming said to Bing, "If I cure the Madame's illness, may she join the feast?"
translations.idiomatic: Bing's family was at dinner; Keming asked him, "If I cure your wife's illness, may she join the meal?"

sentences.zh: ”以半硫圓碾生薑調乳香下之，俄起對食如平常。

translations.literal: He crushed fresh ginger with Half-Sulfur Pill and mixed frankincense to administer it; shortly she rose and ate facing them as usual.
translations.idiomatic: He crushed fresh ginger with a Half-Sulfur Pill, mixed in frankincense, and gave it to her; she soon rose and joined the table as if nothing had been wrong.

sentences.zh: 盧州守王安道風禁不語旬日，他醫莫知所為。

translations.literal: Luzhou prefect Wang Andao had wind seizure and could not speak for ten days; other physicians knew not what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Andao, prefect of Luzhou, had been seized by wind paralysis and unable to speak for ten days; other physicians were at a loss.

sentences.zh: 克明令熾炭燒地，灑藥，置安道於上，須臾而蘇。

translations.literal: Keming ordered blazing coals to burn the ground, sprinkled medicine, placed Andao upon it, and in a moment he revived.
translations.idiomatic: Keming had the floor heated with blazing coals, sprinkled it with medicine, and laid Wang Andao upon it; in moments he revived.

sentences.zh: 金使黑鹿穀過姑蘇，病傷寒垂死，克明治之，明日愈。

translations.literal: Jin envoy Heilugu passed through Gusu, fell ill with cold damage and was near death; Keming treated him and the next day he recovered.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin envoy Heilugu fell critically ill with typhoid fever while passing through Gusu; Keming treated him, and he recovered the next day.

sentences.zh: 及從徐度聘金，黑鹿穀適為先排使，待克明厚甚。

translations.literal: When he followed Xu Du on a mission to Jin, Heilugu happened to be advance envoy and treated Keming with great generosity.
translations.idiomatic: When Keming later joined Xu Du on a mission to Jin, Heilugu happened to be the advance envoy and treated him with exceptional generosity.

sentences.zh: 克明訝之，穀乃道其故，由是名聞北方。

translations.literal: Keming was surprised; Gu then told the reason, and thereby his fame spread to the north.
translations.idiomatic: Keming was surprised until Heilugu explained why; from that day his reputation reached the north.

sentences.zh: 後再從呂正己使金，金接伴使忽被危疾，克明立起之，卻其謝。

translations.literal: Later, following Lu Zhengji on another mission to Jin, the Jin receiving envoy suddenly suffered a dangerous illness; Keming immediately raised him up and declined thanks.
translations.idiomatic: On a later mission to Jin with Lu Zhengji, the Jin escort envoy was suddenly stricken with a grave illness; Keming cured him at once and refused reward.

sentences.zh: 張子蓋救海州，戰士大疫，克明時在軍中，全活者幾萬人。

translations.literal: Zhang Zigai relieved Haizhou; the soldiers suffered a great epidemic; Keming was then in the army and those wholly saved numbered nearly ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Zigai fought to relieve Haizhou, the troops were ravaged by epidemic; Keming was with the army and saved nearly ten thousand lives.

sentences.zh: 子蓋上其功，克明力辭之。

translations.literal: Zigai reported his merit upward; Keming forcefully declined it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zigai tried to report his achievements, but Keming firmly refused the credit.

sentences.zh: 克明頗知書，好俠尚義，常數千里赴人之急。

translations.literal: Keming was quite learned in books, loved chivalry and prized righteousness, and often traveled thousands of li to answer others' emergencies.
translations.idiomatic: Keming was well read, devoted to chivalry and righteousness, and often traveled thousands of li to answer someone's urgent call.

sentences.zh: 初試禮部中選，累任醫官。

translations.literal: At first he passed the Ministry of Rites examination and was selected; he served repeatedly as medical official.
translations.idiomatic: He had passed the Ministry of Rites examination in his youth and later held a series of medical posts.

sentences.zh: 王炎宣撫四川，辟克明，不就。

translations.literal: Wang Yan, Pacification Commissioner of Sichuan, recruited Keming, but he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Yan, Pacification Commissioner of Sichuan, tried to recruit him, Keming declined.

sentences.zh: 炎怒，劾克明避事，坐貶秩。

translations.literal: Yan was angered, impeached Keming for shirking duty, and he was demoted in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan was incensed, impeached Keming for evading duty, and had him demoted.

sentences.zh: 後遷至額內翰林醫痊局，賜金紫。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to the quota-position within the Hanlin Medical Bureau and was granted gold seal and purple robe.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to a senior post in the Hanlin Medical Bureau and awarded the gold seal and purple robe.

sentences.zh: 紹興五年卒，年六十七。

translations.literal: He died in the fifth year of Shaoxing, aged sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of Shaoxing at the age of sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 莎衣道人，姓何氏，淮陽軍朐山人。

translations.literal: The Sha-robe Daoist, surname He, was a man of Qushan in Huaiyang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Sha-robe Daoist, surnamed He, was from Qushan in Huaiyang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖執禮，仕至朝議大夫。

translations.literal: His ancestor Zili served up to the rank of Court Discussant Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Zili had risen to the rank of Court Discussant Grandee.

sentences.zh: 道人避亂渡江，嚐舉進士不中。

translations.literal: The Daoist crossed the river fleeing chaos; he once took the Presented Scholar examination but did not pass.
translations.idiomatic: He fled south across the river during the turmoil and once failed the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 紹興末，來平江。

translations.literal: At the end of Shaoxing he came to Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Shaoxing era he arrived in Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 一日，自外歸，倏若狂者，身衣白礻間，晝丐食於市，夜止天慶觀。

translations.literal: One day he returned from outside and suddenly seemed mad; he wore white ramie cloth, begged food in the market by day, and lodged at the Tianqing Abbey by night.
translations.idiomatic: One day he came back from outside and suddenly acted like a madman; dressed in white ramie, he begged in the markets by day and slept at the Tianqing Abbey by night.

sentences.zh: 久之，衣益敝，以莎緝之。

translations.literal: After a long while his clothes grew more tattered, and he patched them with sedge.
translations.idiomatic: In time his clothes wore thinner still, and he patched them with sedge.

sentences.zh: 嚐遊妙嚴寺，臨池見影，豁然大悟。

translations.literal: Once he visited Miaoyan Temple, saw his reflection by a pool, and was suddenly enlightened.
translations.idiomatic: Once at Miaoyan Temple he saw his reflection in a pool and was suddenly enlightened.

sentences.zh: 人無貴賤，問休咎，罔不奇中。

translations.literal: Whether high or low, those who asked about fortune and misfortune found his answers uncannily accurate.
translations.idiomatic: High or low, anyone who asked about fortune or misfortune found his answers uncannily right.

sentences.zh: 會有瘵者乞醫，命持一草去，旬日而愈。

translations.literal: Once a consumptive begged for treatment; he told him to take a certain herb away, and within ten days he recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Once a consumptive asked for treatment; he gave him a single herb to take away, and within ten days the man recovered.

sentences.zh: 眾翕然傳莎草可以愈疾，求而不得者，或遂不起，由是遠近異之。

translations.literal: The crowd agreed that sedge grass could cure illness; those who sought it but could not obtain it sometimes died, and from this he was regarded as strange far and near.
translations.idiomatic: Word spread that his sedge grass could cure disease; those who could not obtain it sometimes died anyway, and from then on he was regarded as extraordinary throughout the region.

sentences.zh: 孝宗一夕夢莎衣人跣哭來吊者，訊之曰：“蘇人也。

translations.literal: One night Emperor Xiaozong dreamed of a barefoot man in a sedge robe coming to wail in mourning; he asked him, and the man said, "I am from Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: One night Emperor Xiaozong dreamed of a barefoot man in a sedge robe coming to mourn; when questioned, the man said, "I am from Suzhou.

sentences.zh: ”詰其故，不肯言。

translations.literal: " When pressed for the reason, he would not speak.
translations.idiomatic: " Pressed for the reason, he would not answer.

sentences.zh: 帝寤，以語內侍。

translations.literal: The emperor awoke and told the palace attendants.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor awoke and told his attendants.

sentences.zh: 會後及太子薨，帝哀泣，內侍進前勉釋，並道前夢。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the empress and crown prince died; the emperor wept in grief, and attendants came forward to console him and related the earlier dream.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the empress and crown prince died; as the emperor wept, attendants came forward to console him and told him of the dream.

sentences.zh: 帝乃矍然，因遣使召之，不至。

translations.literal: The emperor started in alarm and sent envoys to summon him, but he did not come.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor started in alarm and sent envoys to summon him, but he would not come.

sentences.zh: 帝念恢復大計，累歲未有所屬，後位虛且久，乃焚香默言：“何誠能仙顧，必知朕意。

translations.literal: The emperor thought of the great plan of recovery, which for years had lacked a focus, and of the empress's place long vacant; he burned incense and said silently, "If He Cheng can deign to visit as an immortal, he will surely know my mind.
translations.idiomatic: Brooding on the great plan of recovery, which for years had lacked direction, and on the long-vacant empress's throne, he burned incense and murmured, "If He Cheng will favor us with a visit, he must know what is in my heart.

sentences.zh: ”遂遣中官致贄，不言所以。

translations.literal: " He then sent a eunuch with gifts, saying nothing of the purpose.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent a eunuch with gifts, without explaining why.

sentences.zh: 道人見之掉首，吳音曰：“有中國即有外夷；

translations.literal: The Daoist shook his head at the sight and said in a Wu accent, "Where there is China there are outer barbarians;
translations.idiomatic: The Daoist shook his head and said in a Wu accent, "Where there is China there are outer barbarians;

sentences.zh: 有日即有月，不須問。

translations.literal: where there is sun there is moon—there is no need to ask.
translations.idiomatic: where there is sun there is moon—no need to ask.

sentences.zh: ”趣之去。

translations.literal: " He urged them to leave.
translations.idiomatic: " He urged them away.

sentences.zh: 使者歸奏，帝甚異之，遂賜號通神先生，為築庵觀中，賜衣數襲，皆不受。

translations.literal: The envoys returned and reported; the emperor was greatly struck and granted him the title Master of Penetrating Spirit, built him a hermitage in the abbey, and gave him several suits of clothing—all of which he refused.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoys reported back, the emperor was astonished and granted him the title Master of Penetrating Spirit, built him a hermitage at the abbey, and gave him several suits of clothes—all of which he refused.

sentences.zh: 好事者強邀入庵，大笑而出，復於故處。

translations.literal: Curious onlookers forced him into the hermitage; he laughed loudly and came out, returning to his former place.
translations.idiomatic: Well-wishers dragged him into the hermitage; he laughed loudly, walked out, and went back to his old spot.

sentences.zh: 眾日以珍饌餉之，每食於通衢，逮飽即去。

translations.literal: The crowd daily brought him delicacies; he ate in the public thoroughfare and left as soon as he was full.
translations.idiomatic: People daily brought him delicacies; he ate in the open street and left as soon as he had his fill.

sentences.zh: 帝歲命內侍即其居設十道齋，合雲水之士，施予優普。

translations.literal: Each year the emperor ordered palace attendants to set up ten-way vegetarian feasts at his dwelling, gathering wandering clergy and bestowing generous charity.
translations.idiomatic: Each year the emperor ordered feasts of ten offerings at his dwelling, gathering itinerant clergy and distributing generous alms.

sentences.zh: 一歲，偶逾期，眾鹹訝而請，道人亟起於臥，搖手瞬目而招之曰：“亟來，亟來！

translations.literal: One year the feast ran late; the crowd was astonished and urged him on; the Daoist rose quickly from bed, waved his hand, blinked, and beckoned, saying, "Come quickly, come quickly!
translations.idiomatic: One year the feast was overdue; everyone was astonished and urged him on; the Daoist sprang from bed, waved and winked, and beckoned, crying, "Come quickly, come quickly!

sentences.zh: ”是日內侍至平望，眾益服其神。

translations.literal: " That day the palace attendants reached Pingwang, and the crowd admired his spirit all the more.
translations.idiomatic: " That very day the palace attendants reached Pingwang, and the crowd admired his powers all the more.

sentences.zh: 光宗即位，召之，又不至。

translations.literal: When Guangzong took the throne he was summoned again, but again he did not come.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangzong succeeded, he was summoned again and again refused to come.

sentences.zh: 慶元六年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the sixth year of Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of Qingyuan (1200).

sentences.zh: 孫守榮，臨安富陽人。

translations.literal: Sun Shourong was a native of Fuyang in Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Shourong came from Fuyang in Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 生七歲，病瞽。

translations.literal: At seven he fell ill and went blind.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he fell ill and went blind.

sentences.zh: 遇異人教以風角、鳥占之術，其法以音律推五數，播五行，測度萬物始終盛衰之理。

translations.literal: He met an extraordinary man who taught him wind-angle and bird-omen arts; the method used musical pitch to derive the five numbers, spread them through the five phases, and measured the principles of rise, fall, flourishing, and decline in all things.
translations.idiomatic: He met a strange man who taught him wind-angle and bird-omen divination—a method that used musical pitch to derive the five numbers, spread them through the five phases, and gauge the cycles of growth and decline in all things.

sentences.zh: 凡問者，一語頃，輒知休咎。

translations.literal: For all who asked, within a single phrase he would know fortune or misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever asked him learned their fortune or misfortune within a single phrase.

sentences.zh: 守榮既悟，異人授以鐵笛，遂去不復見。

translations.literal: Once Shourong had understood, the extraordinary man gave him an iron flute and departed, never to be seen again.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shourong had mastered the art, the stranger gave him an iron flute and vanished, never to be seen again.

sentences.zh: 守榮因號富春子，吹笛市中，人初不異也。

translations.literal: Shourong therefore styled himself Master of Fuchun and played his flute in the market; at first people thought nothing of it.
translations.idiomatic: He styled himself Master of Fuchun and played his flute in the markets; at first no one thought him unusual.

sentences.zh: 然其術率驗。

translations.literal: Yet his art was generally accurate.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his predictions usually came true.

sentences.zh: 寶慶間，遊吳興，聞譙樓鼓角聲，驚曰：“旦夕且有變，土人當有典郡者。

translations.literal: During Baoqing he traveled to Wuxing; hearing drum and horn from the watchtower, he exclaimed in alarm, "Before long there will be upheaval, and a local man will become prefect.
translations.idiomatic: During the Baoqing era he visited Wuxing; hearing drums and horns from the watchtower, he cried in alarm, "Trouble is coming soon, and a local man will become prefect.

sentences.zh: ”見王元春，即賀之曰：“作鄉郡者，必君也。

translations.literal: " Seeing Wang Yuanchun, he immediately congratulated him: "The one who will govern this prefecture must be you.
translations.idiomatic: " Seeing Wang Yuanchun, he congratulated him at once: "You will be the one to govern this prefecture.

sentences.zh: ”元春初不之信。

translations.literal: " Yuanchun at first did not believe him.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuanchun did not believe him at first.

sentences.zh: 越兩月，潘丙作亂，元春以告變功，果典郡。

translations.literal: Within two months Pan Bing rebelled; Yuanchun reported the plot and was rewarded with the prefecture, just as predicted.
translations.idiomatic: Two months later Pan Bing rebelled; Yuanchun reported the plot and was made prefect, just as Shourong had said.

sentences.zh: 自是富春子之名大顯，貴人爭延致之。

translations.literal: From then on the name Master of Fuchun became famous, and the eminent vied to invite him.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Master of Fuchun became famous, and the great families competed to invite him.

sentences.zh: 淮南帥李曾伯薦諸朝。

translations.literal: Li Zengbo, military commissioner of Huainan, recommended him to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zengbo, military commissioner of Huainan, recommended him to court.

sentences.zh: 既至，謁丞相史嵩之，閽者以晝寢辭。

translations.literal: When he arrived he called on Chief Councillor Shi Songzhi; the gatekeeper said the minister was napping.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the capital he called on Chief Councillor Shi Songzhi; the gatekeeper said the minister was napping.

sentences.zh: 守榮曰：“丞相方釣魚園池，何得雲爾。

translations.literal: Shourong said, "The chief councillor is fishing in his garden pool—how can you say such a thing?
translations.idiomatic: Shourong said, "The chief councillor is fishing in his garden pool—how can you say he is asleep?

sentences.zh: ”閽者驚異，入白丞相，丞相一見，頗喜之。

translations.literal: " The gatekeeper was startled, went in to report, and on first meeting the chief councillor was quite pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: " The gatekeeper was astonished, went in to report, and on meeting Shourong the chief councillor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 自是數出入相府。

translations.literal: From then on he went in and out of the chief councillor's mansion many times.
translations.idiomatic: After that he came and went from the chief councillor's mansion frequently.

sentences.zh: 一日，庭鵲噪，令占之，曰：“來日晡時，當有寶物至。

translations.literal: One day magpies clamored in the courtyard; ordered to divine, he said, "Tomorrow at the hour of shen a treasure will arrive.
translations.idiomatic: One day magpies clamored in the courtyard; asked to divine, he said, "Tomorrow at the hour of shen a treasure will arrive.

sentences.zh: ”明日，李全果以玉柱斧為貢。

translations.literal: " The next day Li Quan indeed presented a jade-handled battle-axe as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: " The next day Li Quan indeed presented a jade-handled battle-axe as tribute.

sentences.zh: 嵩之又嚐得李全檄藏袖中，詢其事，守榮曰：“此李全詐假布囊二十萬爾。

translations.literal: Songzhi once obtained a dispatch from Li Quan hidden in his sleeve and asked about it; Shourong said, "This is Li Quan's ruse—a false claim of two hundred thousand bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Songzhi once had a dispatch from Li Quan hidden in his sleeve and asked about it; Shourong said, "This is Li Quan's trick—a false claim of two hundred thousand bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: ”剝封，果如其說。

translations.literal: " When the seal was broken open, it was exactly as he said.
translations.idiomatic: " When the seal was broken, it was exactly as he had said.

sentences.zh: 士大夫鹹詢履曆，守榮不盡答。

translations.literal: Scholar-officials all asked about his background, but Shourong did not fully answer.
translations.idiomatic: Scholar-officials all asked about his past, but Shourong would not tell them everything.

sentences.zh: 私謂所知曰：“吾以音推諸朝紳，互有贏縮，宋祿其殆終乎！

translations.literal: Privately he told those he trusted, "By sound I have calculated the court gentlemen—each has gain and loss; the fortune of Song is nearly spent!
translations.idiomatic: Privately he told those he trusted, "By sound I have read the court gentlemen—each rises and falls in turn; the Song dynasty's fortune is nearly spent!

sentences.zh: ”後為嵩之所忌，誣以他罪，貶死遠郡。

translations.literal: " Later, resented by Songzhi, he was falsely charged with another crime and died in exile in a distant prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " Later Songzhi came to resent him; he was falsely charged with another crime and died in exile in a distant prefecture.
